#### A build worker's shared build cache is bounded

_Packages:_ 🟢 _leptoskit_cloud_worker_

_Owner:_ Ifiok Jr. · _Introduced in:_ [e5fee56](https://github.com/leptoskit/leptoskit/commit/e5fee56762346d7604212ec733e30dcd273bca21)

A build worker keeps each project's build cache on one volume that every organisation whose builds run on the worker shares. Nothing capped a cache and nothing removed another project's, so one build with a large layer could fill the volume, and every organisation's next build then failed for want of space until someone deleted directories by hand.

Now a cache export larger than `--build-cache-max-mib` is removed once its build has succeeded. Before each build, the caches of other projects that no build has used for `--build-cache-idle-days` are removed, then the least recently used until no more than `--build-cache-max-used-percent` of the volume is taken. A build never removes the cache of the project it builds, and no build's result changes: a build whose cache was removed is only slower next time.

#### Console pages can't be framed by another site

_Packages:_ 🟢 _leptoskit_cloud_app_

_Owner:_ Ifiok Jr. · _Introduced in:_ [81054a0](https://github.com/leptoskit/leptoskit/commit/81054a09cf174adcc8509131104b170f42054055)

The console sent no `frame-ancestors` policy with its pages, so a site on the console's own domain could show a console page inside a frame. Tenant apps are served on the apps domain, and nothing keeps that domain off the console's site: the example configurations put both on `example.com`. A browser then sends the console's session cookie to the framed page, and one click inside the frame approves a terminal on `/device`, signs out a device on `/account`, or resets an organisation's spend cap.

Every page the console answers with now carries `Content-Security-Policy: frame-ancestors 'none'`, with `X-Content-Type-Options: nosniff` and `Referrer-Policy: no-referrer`, so a browser refuses to draw the page in a frame. The pages the control plane answers itself, which the console's own middleware never sees, get `frame-ancestors 'none'` too, added to a policy the page already sets.

- **The crate compiles for `wasm32` again: the crate root's `Listener` re-export was illegal on that target, where the item comes from the browser module rather than the native fallback, and an extension-style listener helper nothing called is gone.** `Registration::wait_until_active` waits for a registration's own worker to activate — unlike `ready`, which waits for the page's — and errors when the install fails or never settles instead of hanging. `PushSubscription` reports the application server key its subscription was created for, and `PushManager::unsubscribe_endpoint` unsubscribes a registration's current subscription only when it is one named endpoint, so whatever replaced it is never destroyed.
  _Packages:_ 🟢 _leptoskit_service_worker_
  _Owner:_ Ifiok Jr. · _Introduced in:_ [b782f13](https://github.com/leptoskit/leptoskit/commit/b782f1372a8b11ae1338a003c937282609188021)
- **`leptoskit native build` for Android reports the APK size from the app's own `android/` project.** It was still looking under `hosts/android`, so a build that produced an APK said there was nothing to measure.
  _Packages:_ 🟢 _leptoskit_cli_
  _Owner:_ Ifiok Jr. · _Introduced in:_ [a8fec99](https://github.com/leptoskit/leptoskit/commit/a8fec995896be1fea532ee589dfb8869c28f1df7)
- **Keep Android plugins' native libraries on the JNI link line when Cargo prints coloured output, including AAudio for audio plugins.**
  _Packages:_ 🟢 _leptoskit_cli_
  _Owner:_ Ifiok Jr. · _Introduced in:_ [7237130](https://github.com/leptoskit/leptoskit/commit/723713098b125431f6e762cbf4b6f3ebe5506a23)
#### Android and Apple hosts ship every view they draw

_Packages:_ 🟢 _leptoskit_cli_

_Owner:_ Ifiok Jr. · _Introduced in:_ [6f7114d](https://github.com/leptoskit/leptoskit/commit/6f7114d8355acef2a1e98cba223a58c5a7a15f5b)

Generated Android projects now compile: the platform inventories include `NativeCamera.kt`, `NativeMap.kt`, `NativeLivePhoto.kt`, and `NativeServiceWakeBroker.kt`, so `NativeWidgetRenderer` and `LeptosKitView` resolve the views they draw and the background wake they install. The macOS and iOS inventories likewise include `NativeCamera.swift`, `NativeMap.swift`, and `NativeLivePhoto.swift`, which their widget renderers already used.

A test now fails when a shipped Kotlin or Swift source refers to a type declared only in a file the platform inventory leaves out, so this class of missing source is caught before Gradle or Xcode sees it.

- **Android plugin builds read rustc's `native-static-libs` note even when Cargo colors it.** A colored `note:` label was skipped, so the generated CMake link line omitted libraries rustc named, including `aaudio` and `OpenSLES`, and the plugin failed to link.
  _Packages:_ 🟢 _leptoskit_cli_
  _Owner:_ Ifiok Jr. · _Introduced in:_ [f5104c6](https://github.com/leptoskit/leptoskit/commit/f5104c6f382ac2e42b512fb160280ee8d375cb9e)
#### Android hosts link the libraries their plugins need

_Packages:_ 🟢 _leptoskit_cli_

_Owner:_ Ifiok Jr. · _Introduced in:_ [c0c5013](https://github.com/leptoskit/leptoskit/commit/c0c5013b708e17723cb48062036b40f22f694a57)

Generated Android and Quest projects now link. The host's `CMakeLists.txt` names the Rust archive and a fixed list of NDK libraries, and a static archive carries none of Cargo's link directives, so a plugin whose Rust code uses a platform library outside that list failed at `ld.lld` with undefined symbols — `AAudio_createStreamBuilder` and its neighbours once the audio plugin was selected.

The Android host build now asks rustc for the libraries the archive needs (`cargo rustc -- --print native-static-libs`) and writes them into the generated link line, in rustc's order and without repeats, so any plugin's libraries (`aaudio`, `OpenSLES`, `mediandk`, `camera2ndk`, `EGL`, `GLESv3`, `vulkan`, …) arrive with the plugin rather than with a list the CLI has to keep in step.

- **An Android build points cc-rs at the NDK's `llvm-ranlib`, as it already did for `llvm-ar`.** A dependency that builds a vendored OpenSSL through `make` no longer fails with `aarch64-linux-android-ranlib: not found` on machines without `llvm-ranlib` on `PATH`.
  _Packages:_ 🟢 _leptoskit_cli_
  _Owner:_ Ifiok Jr. · _Introduced in:_ [d163d4c](https://github.com/leptoskit/leptoskit/commit/d163d4ce01a3de4209f807b028ade3ed6cf7df1c)
- **Keep the Android API level in native C and C++ builds when a compiler cache wraps the NDK launcher.**
  _Packages:_ 🟢 _leptoskit_cli_
  _Owner:_ Ifiok Jr. · _Introduced in:_ [7237130](https://github.com/leptoskit/leptoskit/commit/723713098b125431f6e762cbf4b6f3ebe5506a23)
- **Refuse graph-root auth generation before writes.** Auth generation checks that it is running in an application configuration before writing client screens or dependency features. Deployment graph roots now fail before any generation writes, including with `--force`, instead of rejecting the application-only auth settings after partially changing a workspace client.
  _Packages:_ 🟢 _leptoskit_cli_
  _Owner:_ Ifiok Jr. · _Introduced in:_ [ac480c5](https://github.com/leptoskit/leptoskit/commit/ac480c5935b3132c20821e2b5143b1e3e5c884fe)
- **Generate auth in the selected backend package.** Auth generation follows `build.server_package`, including a named target's resolved backend, while keeping client selection independent. It defaults to `app.name` when no server package is configured. The generator no longer writes server modules or dependency features into an unselected package that happens to share the application's name.
  _Packages:_ 🟢 _leptoskit_cli_
  _Owner:_ Ifiok Jr. · _Introduced in:_ [3bfdd7f](https://github.com/leptoskit/leptoskit/commit/3bfdd7fec9c797b7262acefce6264a7124887ef8)
- **Reading a watched file does not restart the app.** `leptoskit dev` ignores filesystem access events before scheduling a rebuild or marking the configuration, database tables, or Git branch as changed. On Linux, the compiler and CLI reading their inputs could otherwise trigger another build repeatedly, even without an edit. Source edits and file replacements still rebuild the app.
  _Packages:_ 🟢 _leptoskit_cli_
  _Owner:_ Ifiok Jr. · _Introduced in:_ [60ff4c1](https://github.com/leptoskit/leptoskit/commit/60ff4c128909e3837a936d04e92b4037c58cb14e)
- **Validate the dev address before watching the workspace.** `leptoskit dev` rejects an invalid web serve address before inspecting Cargo metadata, starting a database, or watching files. Watching still begins before the initial build, so edits made during that build trigger a rebuild.
  _Packages:_ 🟢 _leptoskit_cli_
  _Owner:_ Ifiok Jr. · _Introduced in:_ [7237130](https://github.com/leptoskit/leptoskit/commit/723713098b125431f6e762cbf4b6f3ebe5506a23)
- **Flush the development watcher announcement so processes reading piped logs receive it before the initial build finishes.**
  _Packages:_ 🟢 _leptoskit_cli_
  _Owner:_ Ifiok Jr. · _Introduced in:_ [94cd633](https://github.com/leptoskit/leptoskit/commit/94cd633355dffb56cc7249e234ea5fc994c9ba20)
- **`lk dev` keeps edits made while it starts.** `leptoskit dev` now starts watching your project before its first build rather than after every platform has started. An edit saved while that first build ran, which takes minutes on a fresh checkout, used to go unseen: the server came up on the code from before the edit and stayed on it until you saved again. The edit now waits in the watcher's queue, and `dev` rebuilds and restarts the server as soon as the platforms are up. The `watching … for changes` line still prints once everything has started.
  _Packages:_ 🟢 _leptoskit_cli_
  _Owner:_ Ifiok Jr. · _Introduced in:_ [fa3d29f](https://github.com/leptoskit/leptoskit/commit/fa3d29f8e8c837b19f92f1e9a95f699803543767)
- **`leptoskit dev` says it is watching as soon as the watcher is running, before the first build.** That build can take minutes, and the message used to wait until the platforms had started, so an edit during it looked ignored.
  _Packages:_ 🟢 _leptoskit_cli_
  _Owner:_ Ifiok Jr. · _Introduced in:_ [f5104c6](https://github.com/leptoskit/leptoskit/commit/f5104c6f382ac2e42b512fb160280ee8d375cb9e)
- **Image builds retry their tool download.** The Dockerfile that `leptoskit deploy` generates for web apps downloads binaryen's `wasm-opt` from GitHub. It now retries that download up to five times and unpacks it only once it is complete, so a brief GitHub outage no longer fails the image build.
  _Packages:_ 🟢 _leptoskit_cli_
  _Owner:_ Ifiok Jr. · _Introduced in:_ [3cd7307](https://github.com/leptoskit/leptoskit/commit/3cd7307fbdba2e00927bf057a258097652aefca7)
- **Builder lint keeps the SSR shell; apps pin Rust.** `markup = "builder"` no longer reports ordinary HTML tags in the SSR document `shell` (`<html>`, `<head>`, …)—only leptoskit component trees. The agent skill and linting guide say the same. Deploy generation names `--sdk-path` when a path dependency sits outside the workspace. (New apps already pin `rust-toolchain.toml` from the matching scaffold work.)
  _Packages:_ 🟢 _leptoskit_cli_, 🟢 _leptoskit_lint_
  _Owner:_ Ifiok Jr. · _Introduced in:_ [d6f5489](https://github.com/leptoskit/leptoskit/commit/d6f5489be53cd5b202bfd0f8476839a9ce508d41) · _Last updated in:_ [442b38b](https://github.com/leptoskit/leptoskit/commit/442b38b81352231ebb9810f646247bd548ed353c)
#### Generated sign-in effects run in native apps

_Packages:_ 🟢 _leptoskit_cli_

_Owner:_ Ifiok Jr. · _Introduced in:_ [1bd0618](https://github.com/leptoskit/leptoskit/commit/1bd0618c284e4dff885524d3d6a23db9cfc668f8)

`leptoskit new --auth` and `leptoskit generate auth` now use isomorphic effects for the sign-in screen's mount step, the provider-notice step, and the post-sign-in navigation. `Effect::new` is compiled out in a native guest (the generated app does not enable leptos's `effects` feature), so the screen could stay on "Checking whether you're signed in…" forever. The effects still skip server rendering, so the first server HTML matches the browser's first render.

The generated notes journey is now exercised end to end in the real interpreter: the optimized guest loads and refreshes notes over the HTTP plugin, validates the draft, shows pending/saved/failed saves, signs in through the development mailbox, switches accounts without showing the previous account's rows, and rejects late list and save replies after their screen is disposed.

The generated `add_note` operation trims the body before it checks the note's length, so a direct API caller cannot store a note that is only whitespace even though the screen already trims its draft.

The sign-in countdown is tested apart from its executor: a host timer counts the whole wait down, a missing or rejected timer leaves the server's message and a usable manual retry without claiming time passed, a newer refusal or starting over stops an older countdown, and disposing the screen stops it without touching a disposed signal.

`leptoskit generate auth` on an existing database app still adds the screens and asks the app to call `auth::provide()` and put `auth::screens().gate(…)` in front of its own home screen. Rewriting an app's root automatically is not safe, so that manual step stays open; the journey covers the fully scaffolded `--auth` app, which is already wired.

- **Wait for Caddy to finish executing under its dedicated account before checking graph release readiness.** Recheck process identity and socket ownership after probing so systemd startup and process replacement cannot produce premature restoration or a false ready result.
  _Packages:_ 🟢 _leptoskit_cli_
  _Owner:_ Ifiok Jr. · _Introduced in:_ [7c788ae](https://github.com/leptoskit/leptoskit/commit/7c788ae0d8522dc8f0576961ef4bcb9121603f70)
- **Allow protected systemd drop-in masks that point exactly to /dev/null during graph release and recovery.** Active overrides and masks with unsafe ownership or parents remain rejected.
  _Packages:_ 🟢 _leptoskit_cli_
  _Owner:_ Ifiok Jr. · _Introduced in:_ [7c788ae](https://github.com/leptoskit/leptoskit/commit/7c788ae0d8522dc8f0576961ef4bcb9121603f70)
- **Keep graph verification checks portable.** Graph directory creation only mutates its builder when applying Unix permissions. On other hosts, descriptor capability methods retain their instance API and continue refusing operations that require Unix metadata. Windows Clippy no longer rejects these unsupported-platform branches.
  _Packages:_ 🟢 _leptoskit_cli_
  _Owner:_ Ifiok Jr. · _Introduced in:_ [7c788ae](https://github.com/leptoskit/leptoskit/commit/7c788ae0d8522dc8f0576961ef4bcb9121603f70)
- **The generated iOS `App.swift` now imports `LeptosKitNotifications` under its `canImport` guard: the app delegate referenced the plugin's broker type whenever the notifications plugin was selected, but no module was imported, so the generated project failed to compile with the plugin present.** A macOS test now generates the project both with and without the plugin, builds the plugin's Swift package for the iOS simulator, and typechecks the generated app sources — template, registrant, and the bridge's mobile sources — against the real modules, so the conditional import is proven both ways instead of textually.
  _Packages:_ 🟢 _leptoskit_cli_
  _Owner:_ Ifiok Jr. · _Introduced in:_ [b782f13](https://github.com/leptoskit/leptoskit/commit/b782f1372a8b11ae1338a003c937282609188021)
- **`lk lint` passes on a fresh clone.** `leptoskit lint` no longer fails on a fresh clone of an app with native platforms. App-owned runners include a registrant under `.leptoskit/<platform>/`, which Git ignores and only native builds wrote, so clippy stopped on the missing file until you ran a native build. Before clippy starts, `lk lint` now writes missing registrants for the enabled hosts that compile on the current machine and enables the Cargo features their plugins need. Existing registrants stay untouched until the next native build. If a host cannot be prepared, lint reports a warning and clippy names what it cannot compile.
  _Packages:_ 🟢 _leptoskit_cli_
  _Owner:_ Ifiok Jr. · _Introduced in:_ [a7d277c](https://github.com/leptoskit/leptoskit/commit/a7d277c8d7e0b13b2ad4eb084b8aac83b312577c)
- **Cloud tools on `lk mcp` take no `url`.** The `lk mcp` cloud tools (`cloud_estimate`, `cloud_deploy`, `cloud_status`, `cloud_logs`, `cloud_secrets_list`) take no `url` argument. It came from the model or the client, and with `LEPTOSKIT_CLOUD_TOKEN` set one tool call could send that token to any origin the argument named. The tools now choose the cloud as `lk cloud` does without `--url`: `LEPTOSKIT_CLOUD_URL`, then `[cloud].url` in `leptoskit.toml`, then the hosted cloud. The token still goes only to the hosted cloud or to the origin `LEPTOSKIT_CLOUD_URL` names; when `leptoskit.toml` alone points somewhere else, the tool refuses and says to set `LEPTOSKIT_CLOUD_URL`.
  _Packages:_ 🟢 _leptoskit_cli_
  _Owner:_ Ifiok Jr. · _Introduced in:_ [637cdc4](https://github.com/leptoskit/leptoskit/commit/637cdc48582dd612b257fb3728c590854bc56a86)
- **Always run the repository's full pre-push gate, including pushes whose commits change no files.** The gate no longer depends on the hook runner selecting at least one changed file.
  _Packages:_ 🟢 _leptoskit_cli_
  _Owner:_ Ifiok Jr. · _Introduced in:_ [2c909d1](https://github.com/leptoskit/leptoskit/commit/2c909d10b5be31f521b4ea361a62a4f685538894)
- **Release web builds minify the JavaScript glue, its snippets, and the chunk loader with esbuild, next to `wasm-opt`.** Export names and `import.meta` stay, so the page's imports keep working. `esbuild` comes with the development environment; a machine without it can set `bundle.wasm_opt = false` to skip both.
  _Packages:_ 🟢 _leptoskit_cli_
  _Owner:_ Ifiok Jr. · _Introduced in:_ [f5104c6](https://github.com/leptoskit/leptoskit/commit/f5104c6f382ac2e42b512fb160280ee8d375cb9e)
- **New apps write builder lint to match the starter screens.** `leptoskit new` now sets `[lint] markup = "builder"` with `markup_style` and `component_attribute` denied, so a fresh scaffold's builder home screen is clean under `leptoskit lint --deny-warnings`. The skill, creating guide, linting guide, and small-bundles guide match: omitted `render` still defaults to csr in the schema, but new projects keep the explicit ssr they already write.
  _Packages:_ 🟢 _leptoskit_cli_
  _Owner:_ Ifiok Jr. · _Introduced in:_ [5d86470](https://github.com/leptoskit/leptoskit/commit/5d86470b55f2b640a68a13c6097503dc23cfea84)
- **Generated servers find `LeptoskitConfig` again.** The database and auth server templates read `[rpc]` through `leptoskit::LeptoskitConfig`, which `leptoskit` exports only from `leptoskit::config` and its prelude, so a newly generated project didn't compile. They now name `leptoskit::config::LeptoskitConfig`.
  _Packages:_ 🟢 _leptoskit_cli_
  _Owner:_ Ifiok Jr. · _Introduced in:_ [ef5e7c5](https://github.com/leptoskit/leptoskit/commit/ef5e7c58952db616d3de126653148ae14add82a0)
- **Scaffold uses shared Health; skill documents web-only trim.** New apps re-export `Health` from the shared crate in the app library so `leptoskit lint --deny-warnings` no longer fails on an unused `*_shared` dependency before any RPC types are used. The coding-agent skill says there is no frontend-only `new` flag: after scaffolding, set `platforms = ["web"]` and optionally trim unused host workspace members.
  _Packages:_ 🟢 _leptoskit_cli_
  _Owner:_ Ifiok Jr. · _Introduced in:_ [fb5e435](https://github.com/leptoskit/leptoskit/commit/fb5e4353ff93ff3cfed5eab0a9d01997609c2bad)
- **New apps pin rustc; skill matches the scaffold.** `leptoskit new` now writes a `rust-toolchain.toml` that pins the SDK channel and the `wasm32-unknown-unknown` target, so `edition = "2024"` projects build even when rustup's default toolchain is older. The coding-agent skill no longer claims the default starter uses regenerating file routes, tells agents to keep the HTML `shell` in leptos `view!` (with a line-local lint allow) when enforcing builders, and shows `#[component]` helpers returning `Element` for `.child(…)` composition. The creating guide notes the SSR default and the toolchain pin.
  _Packages:_ 🟢 _leptoskit_cli_
  _Owner:_ Ifiok Jr. · _Introduced in:_ [53ca740](https://github.com/leptoskit/leptoskit/commit/53ca7405fac9fb680cd7468429cf09d9b004e76e) · _Last updated in:_ [442b38b](https://github.com/leptoskit/leptoskit/commit/442b38b81352231ebb9810f646247bd548ed353c)
- **Web-only lint skips unused hosts; drop an import.** `leptoskit lint`'s clippy pass excludes workspace host crates whose platforms are not listed in `app.platforms`, so setting `platforms = ["web"]` is enough for a green deny-warnings run without GTK or native prepare. `--db` / `--auth` scaffolds no longer put an unused `use leptos::prelude::*` in `App()`. The skill documents the platforms-based clippy skip.
  _Packages:_ 🟢 _leptoskit_cli_
  _Owner:_ Ifiok Jr. · _Introduced in:_ [44be954](https://github.com/leptoskit/leptoskit/commit/44be9542fedde87deb6c823b8c7f3f5ad44cc49d) · _Last updated in:_ [442b38b](https://github.com/leptoskit/leptoskit/commit/442b38b81352231ebb9810f646247bd548ed353c)
- **`lk lint` knows the plugin surface tags.** `lk lint` now counts the plugin surfaces `Video`, `Camera`, `Map`, and `LivePhoto` among leptoskit's built-in components, so the markup-style rule checks trees that use them like any other built-in tag.
  _Packages:_ 🟢 _leptoskit_lint_
  _Owner:_ Ifiok Jr. · _Introduced in:_ [b4efffc](https://github.com/leptoskit/leptoskit/commit/b4efffc4eb47c86b523454bfc2508c0fcd97a1e1)
- **Over the air updates get their own section.** The home page and README now lead with one component tree and real native widgets. Over-the-air updates have their own section, describing code push for installed native apps and which generated hosts install releases.
  _Packages:_ 🟢 _leptoskit_
  _Owner:_ Ifiok Jr. · _Introduced in:_ [8a98548](https://github.com/leptoskit/leptoskit/commit/8a98548690f1654a63c9b6adffe8b603ba3bbfb5)
#### Check independent consumers before crate publication

_Packages:_ 🟢 _leptoskit_

_Owner:_ Ifiok Jr. · _Introduced in:_ [b6a1990](https://github.com/leptoskit/leptoskit/commit/b6a1990a574a7c077e4f31d408550ae64045a016)

Compile eight separate browser, guest, server and auth feature combinations from the actual Cargo package payloads before publication. Require complete package resolution and reject server features in client builds. Retain per-consumer build logs and exact archive and lockfile hashes; failed or incomplete runs produce no successful acceptance report.

Reject archive paths and directory names that alias by case on every host, so Linux validation also catches archives that cannot extract on a case-insensitive filesystem.

Run validation during release dry runs without publisher credentials. Before upload, require freshly prepared archives to match the hashes from the successful consumer run on the same revision.

- **Fix the platform module guide's path from the source root.** The creating-an-app guide now uses `components/heading` for a module in `src/components/heading.rs`, matching `platform_module!`'s source-root-relative paths. The generated application's end-to-end test uses the same corrected declaration and still verifies adding and removing a platform override.
  _Packages:_ 🟢 _leptoskit_
  _Owner:_ Ifiok Jr. · _Introduced in:_ [d9a66d1](https://github.com/leptoskit/leptoskit/commit/d9a66d1e73141c14be24d3e57bcd4f1cf600bdca)

sections.title: Features
entries:
#### Ask a provider to sign in again

_Owner:_ Ifiok Jr. · _Introduced in:_ [f25ea8c](https://github.com/leptoskit/leptoskit/commit/f25ea8c94f5875355ce081afae5ac92a652cee48)

`StartProvider` has a `prompt` field. `Some(Prompt::Login)` asks the provider to sign the person in again even when someone is already signed in there, which is how a person switches to another account. `Some(Prompt::SelectAccount)` shows the provider's account picker. The value reaches the provider's authorization page as OpenID Connect's `prompt` parameter, and a provider that doesn't know the parameter ignores it.

```rust
sign_in.mutate(StartProvider {
	provider: "main".into(),
	redirect_to: Some("/admin/sign-in".into()),
	prompt: Some(Prompt::Login),
});
```

Code that builds a `StartProvider` needs `prompt: None` to keep today's behaviour.

#### CanvistEditor: a place for a canvist text editor

_Owner:_ Ifiok Jr. · _Introduced in:_ [5c71502](https://github.com/leptoskit/leptoskit/commit/5c71502b830239c1bcbf9301497142aa2003aa9a)

`CanvistEditor(id)` is a new element, with its own `NativeKind::CanvistEditor`, that marks where a [canvist](https://github.com/canvist/canvist) text editor shows. The app owns the editor through a state handle and gives the element the handle's id, so the document never travels through props. `placeholder`, `read_only`, and an accessible label work as on a `TextArea`, and the element must have a name like any text field.

This change adds only the place. On the web the element renders an empty `<div data-lk-canvist-editor="id">` that the editor's host looks for, and a server-rendered page names the browser's own editor on it when it hydrates; the host is the experimental, unpublished `leptoskit_canvist` crate, and the `leptoskit` component that joins the two comes next. macOS, iOS, Android, Linux, and Windows show an empty view, the terminal a dim block, and the watch surfaces refuse the element. The Swift and Kotlin renderers that generated apps use show an empty view too; the Swift ones used to stop on a kind they did not know.

The wire name is `canvist_editor`, appended last in the wire kind table, so existing codes keep their meaning.

#### Add ergonomic platform features and capability catalog

_Owner:_ Ifiok Jr. · _Introduced in:_ [65c9b66](https://github.com/leptoskit/leptoskit/commit/65c9b66b6d97b26fece49f1003ceb73cb80ae59a) · _Last updated in:_ [2a8294b](https://github.com/leptoskit/leptoskit/commit/2a8294b2f569ff7f1f1bd7d7035e458aa06c0a8c)

Expose opt-in Cargo features on `leptoskit` (`live-activities`, `home-widgets`, `app-shortcuts`, `android-intent`, `menu`, `window-state`, `updater`, plus the `mobile-surfaces` and `desktop-extras` bundles) that re-export those plugins under `leptoskit::platform::*` and forward `leptoskit/guest`.

Expand `leptoskit_native::target::Capability` with exhaustive iOS and Android OS capabilities (including both wired built-in plugins and transparent entries for OS capabilities not yet wired as native plugins), along with `Capability::ALL`, `as_str()`, `plugin_crate()`, `runtime_plugin_name()`, `cargo_feature()`, `has_builtin_plugin()`, `summary()`, `TargetPlatform::supports()`, `PlatformCapabilities::supported_capabilities()`, and `PlatformCapabilities::available_capabilities()`.

#### Move keyboard focus once with `FocusRequest`

_Owner:_ Ifiok Jr. · _Introduced in:_ [f9752b8](https://github.com/leptoskit/leptoskit/commit/f9752b87d178230e24d89cb8df527e6f7e9518b6)

`FocusRequest::new()` makes a `Copy` handle. Give it to a widget with `focus_on(request)` and call `request()` from any handler: focus moves to that widget once, after the screen next updates, and later updates leave focus where the person has since put it. Use it to land in the code field after a code is sent, to return to the button that opened a menu, or to put a screen reader on an error summary. `focused(true)` is unchanged and still suits a widget that should always hold focus.

It works on every backend: `focus()` on the web (text and containers get `tabindex="-1"` so they can take it), the focus ring in the terminal, `grab_focus` on GTK, first responder on macOS and iOS, `SetFocus` on Windows and `requestFocus` on Android. Where a platform has no keyboard focus for a widget, iOS and Android move the VoiceOver or TalkBack cursor instead, and macOS and Windows leave focus alone. On macOS, Windows, iOS and Android the widget does not hear a `Focus` event for a requested move.

Renderer authors: `NativeProps` gains `focus_request`. `NativeSurface` sends it only with the commit that makes a new request, so a backend focuses `MutationList::focus_target()` after applying a batch and keeps no state.

- **Gestures on a view.** A view can follow a finger. `gesture(Gesture::tap())`, `pan`, `long_press`, `pinch`, `rotation`, and `fling` recognize the pointer in one arena shared by the Android widget backend and Linux. `simultaneous`, `exclusive`, and `race` compose recognizers the way a pinch and a rotation share one gesture, or a pan wins over a tap. A drag that wins claims the pointer so the control underneath does not also click. A tap does not, so a button still presses. iOS, macOS, Windows, the web, the terminal, and the generated Swift and Kotlin renderers still deliver presses and clicks only.
  _Owner:_ Ifiok Jr. · _Introduced in:_ [955a1bf](https://github.com/leptoskit/leptoskit/commit/955a1bf7d00666992a8ccd52032131c7ae97cca1)

#### A field's label focuses it on the web

_Owner:_ Ifiok Jr. · _Introduced in:_ [0170294](https://github.com/leptoskit/leptoskit/commit/0170294ffef2da84f21c303fb7859fc8eec160e8)

A `Text` that names a field through `aria_labelled_by` now renders as `<label for="…">` on the web, so a click on the label focuses a `TextInput`, `PasswordInput`, `TextArea` or `Slider` and toggles a `Checkbox`, `Switch` or `Radio`, with no handler and no script. It applies when the field has an `id`, is named by exactly one plain `Text`, and no other field is named after the same text. `leptoskit_aria::Field` and `leptoskit::form` already build this shape. The markup for such a text changes from `<span>` to `<label>`; its styles and its `id` stay the same.

On Android, the label's view gets `labelFor`, so TalkBack knows which field it names. Other platforms are unchanged: clicking a label is not a convention there, and the field already carries the label's text as its name.

#### Open links in a new tab, save them, or open them natively

_Owner:_ Ifiok Jr. · _Introduced in:_ [e5e6912](https://github.com/leptoskit/leptoskit/commit/e5e6912ebad6fcc21582314d0aa6355cca54c554)

A `Pressable` link can now say where it opens and whether it is a download.

```rust
Pressable("Open the admin")
	.href("https://admin.example.com/")
	.target(LinkTarget::NewTab)
	.child(Text("Open the admin ↗"));

Pressable("Export").href("/people/7/export").download("person-7.json");
```

On the web, `LinkTarget::NewTab` renders `target="_blank" rel="noopener noreferrer"` and tells screen reader users the link opens in a new tab. `download(name)` renders `<a href download>`, so the browser saves the file under that name. A name that is not one plain file name is ignored.

Native apps used to ignore `href`. With the new `links` feature, pressing a link that has no `on_press` handler opens an absolute HTTP(S), `mailto:`, `tel:` or `sms:` link outside the app, through `leptoskit_plugin_linking`: directly on macOS, Windows and Linux, and through the host's `linking` plugin in a Wasm guest on iOS and Android. A link with a handler, a relative link and a disabled link behave as before.

- **Person attributes, segments, and send to everyone.** The service keeps a registry of the people it knows — registered when the app's server sets their attributes, when they subscribe to a topic, set a category preference, or enroll a push endpoint, and backfilled from those tables by the migration; a person named only in a recipients send is never registered. The app's server describes people with `set_person_attributes` (batch, ≤1,000 people, idempotent; keys `a-z0-9_` ≤64 bytes, values ≤256 bytes, ≤50 attributes per person with cap-skipping counted; `person_attributes` reads back; `forget_person` removes the person from the registry with their attributes and topic subscriptions, keeping their inbox) — app-only by design, so a segment can't be forged from the client side. The condition grammar extends FCM's with `user.<key> == 'v'`, `!=`, `in ['a','b']`, `has(user.<key>)`, and finite-number `<`, `<=`, `>`, `>=` (true only when both sides parse as finite numbers; `NaN`/`inf` literals refused), mixing freely with `'t' in topics` under `&&`/`||`/`!`/parens with byte-offset errors and bounds (≤5 topics, ≤10 attribute predicates, depth ≤8, ≤1 KiB); an absent attribute answers false to every predicate, and the everyone-in-disguise refusal now checks topics _and_ attributes. `SendTarget::Everyone` reaches every registered person, and a condition no longer needs to be anchored on a topic: one that structurally requires a topic still fans out over the topic index, while an attribute-anchored one (and everyone) fans out over the registry — same batched, cursor-advancing, idempotent fanout job, same opt-out/visibility/push/live behaviour, `validate_only` counting every target. SQLite and Postgres migrations add `persons` and `person_attributes` with the registry backfill.
  _Owner:_ Ifiok Jr. · _Introduced in:_ [644b0a3](https://github.com/leptoskit/leptoskit/commit/644b0a354e16352b37cfb3c78934d5c4e5b76a6e)

- **Add `leptoskit_notifications`, the first-party notifications service: an app's server sends idempotently to explicit user ids, and each recipient gets one durable inbox row in the service's own database — scheduled visibility with cancel-before-due, expiry, category opt-outs enforced at send and at visibility, and per-person read and dismissed state shared across devices, read through bounded, live-paginated queries on every platform the app's screens run.** Time reaches open screens: every send enqueues a wake job when it becomes visible and at its expiry, so a scheduled item appears and an expired one leaves a watching screen without any other write; preference changes update open inboxes the same way. An accepted send answers its stored outcome forever, however the clock moves on, and a known zero-fanout send cancels idempotently. Delivery is authenticated inbox retrieval while the app runs; OS background push (APNs, FCM, Web Push) and device enrollment are not part of this change. The `leptoskit` facade re-exports the shared types behind a `notifications` feature, and the guide is under Services.
  _Owner:_ Ifiok Jr. · _Introduced in:_ [b782f13](https://github.com/leptoskit/leptoskit/commit/b782f1372a8b11ae1338a003c937282609188021)

- **Audience partitioning by topics and conditions, with a durable batched fanout.** A send can now target `SendTarget::Topic` or `SendTarget::Condition` beside today's `SendTarget::Recipients`: the app's server subscribes people to per-person topics in idempotent batches (`subscribe_to_topic`/`unsubscribe_from_topic`, at most 1,000 people per call; a person holds at most 500 topics, and a full person is skipped and counted rather than refusing the batch), and a person may subscribe themselves (`subscribe`, `unsubscribe`, `my_topics`, live and paginated) to the topics the operator opened in `LEPTOSKIT_NOTIFICATIONS_OPEN_TOPICS` — patterns like `news.*`, nothing open by default, and the person always read from the forwarded identity. Conditions use FCM's grammar verbatim (`'a' in topics && ('b' in topics || !('c' in topics))`), validated on both sides with byte-offset errors, FCM's bounds (≤5 topics, depth ≤8, ≤1 KiB), and unanchored conditions — ones true for a person holding no topics — refused, since there is no everyone audience. A topic or condition send answers `fanning_out` immediately and a job walks the audience in 500-person batches — one transaction per batch for the inbox rows, push deliveries, and the stored cursor, unique per send and person so a crashed or replayed batch never duplicates, the audience snapshotted as the fanout reaches each person. `send_status` answers the state and counts; `validate_only` counts the audience without writing; `cancel` stops a fanout mid-walk and cancels the rows written so far. SQLite and Postgres migrations add the `topic_subscriptions` table, the fanout bookkeeping on `sends`, and the per-send-per-person uniqueness on `notifications` (existing rows backfilled). Breaking: `Send` and `check_send` take the target — `recipients: vec![…]` becomes `target: SendTarget::Recipients(vec![…])` — and `SendResult` gains `state` and `targeted`.
  _Owner:_ Ifiok Jr. · _Introduced in:_ [ed7b1e7](https://github.com/leptoskit/leptoskit/commit/ed7b1e77bb3ac93482b58819cdad9df80fdaa166)

#### Modal and Popover show content above the screen

_Owner:_ Ifiok Jr. · _Introduced in:_ [08a70cb](https://github.com/leptoskit/leptoskit/commit/08a70cb0dbd8a153b2b8eb285099920fb6d2252c)

`Modal(open)` blocks the screen until it is answered, and `Popover(anchor, open)` hangs from the element with that `id`. Both stay in the tree while closed. `.on_dismiss(...)` hears Escape and a press outside as a request to close, and the overlay closes when the next build says so. `.initial_focus(id)` names what takes focus on opening, and `.placement(Placement::BelowEnd)` picks a popover's side. In `view!` they are `<Modal open=…>` and `<Popover anchor=… open=…>`.

On the web a `Modal` is a `<dialog>` opened with `showModal()` and a `Popover` uses the `popover` attribute, so the browser supplies the top layer, the inert page, the focus trap and focus restore. The terminal draws overlays last, keeps Tab inside an open modal, and gives focus back on close.

macOS, iOS, Android, Linux and Windows draw an overlay as a layer in the right place for now. Nothing asks to dismiss it there, focus is not moved or kept inside, and a parent that clips or scrolls cuts it off.

For backend authors: `NativeKind` gains `Modal` and `Popover`, `NativeEvent` gains `Dismiss`, and `NativeProps` gains `overlay`. A backend that returns `true` from the new `NativeBackend::presents_overlays` is told the real kinds and given open overlays' frames in viewport coordinates. Every other backend is given a `View` with a frame relative to its parent. The guest event ABI gains kind 9 (dismiss), and the bridge event codes gain 10.

#### Add platform targeting and capability queries

_Owner:_ Ifiok Jr. · _Introduced in:_ [fee46c0](https://github.com/leptoskit/leptoskit/commit/fee46c0e80a311139a43d5b33ea3f559aae84df6)

`leptoskit::target` adds a shared runtime and compile-time platform API (`TargetPlatform`, `PlatformFamily`, `PlatformSwitch`, `PlatformCapabilities`, `Capability`, `CapabilitySupport`, `with_platform`, and `on_ios` / `on_android` / `on_mobile` / `on_macos` / `on_windows` / `on_linux` / `on_desktop` / `on_apple` / `on_web` / `on_extension` / `on_watch`) so universal apps can cleanly opt into platform-specific features and test every platform branch from any host.

`leptoskit_build::platforms()` now also recognizes `harmonyos`, `wearos`, `watchos`, and `quest` alongside the existing platform features.

#### Screen state and queries survive a rebuild

_Owner:_ Ifiok Jr. · _Introduced in:_ [c7a85ef](https://github.com/leptoskit/leptoskit/commit/c7a85ef05c4a1a510f6136b444ad4a0c2ef1af5e)

leptoskit builds a screen again whenever a signal it read changes. Two things broke under that: a `RwSignal::new(..)` inside a screen ran again with every rebuild, so a chosen filter or a typed field reset as soon as the screen redrew, and a `use_query` in a screen refetched in a loop, because the rebuild its data caused mounted the query again while the data already counted as stale.

- `leptoskit_native`: `remember(|| initial)` returns the same `RwSignal` on every build of the screen, told apart by its place in the source and by order. `remember_keyed(&key, || initial)` names the value by a key instead, for rows that move. A value is released once a whole build no longer reaches it, such as after navigating to another route. `guest::mount` keeps the values for native apps. In the browser, `web::screen(move || ..)` replaces `move || web::render(..)` and does the same. `ScreenState` is the store underneath, for hosts of their own. Both functions are in `leptoskit::prelude`, and the module is `leptoskit::remember`.
- `leptoskit_query`: a query mounted within two seconds of this client's last fetch of it takes that fetch's data or error instead of fetching again, like SWR's deduping interval. The window covers `RefetchOn::Always` and `retry_on_mount`, and not invalidation, `refetch()`, focus, reconnect, or intervals. Data from `set_query_data`, initial data, or hydration doesn't count as a fetch. Set it with `with_mount_dedupe` on `QueryDefaults`, `QueryOptions`, or `QueryObserverOptions`; `Duration::ZERO` gives TanStack's behaviour. `QueryOptions`, `QueryDefaults`, and `ResolvedQueryOptions` gain a `mount_dedupe` field, so code that builds them with struct literals needs it too.

An app with its own keyed store and a long stale time to work around this can switch to `remember` and drop both.

- **Set the browser tab's title.** `leptoskit_router::set_title("Plans · Admin")` names what the person is looking at. On the web it sets the document's title, so the tab and the history entry follow the screen as the person moves around without a page load. A server-rendered page still writes its first title in its own `<title>`. Native windows keep the title they were opened with for now, and on a phone it does nothing.
  _Owner:_ Ifiok Jr. · _Introduced in:_ [edcb32f](https://github.com/leptoskit/leptoskit/commit/edcb32f5b4424abc33d17a784c8afb896ea06a14)

#### Arrow keys move through tabs and radio cards

_Owner:_ Ifiok Jr. · _Introduced in:_ [bc7c851](https://github.com/leptoskit/leptoskit/commit/bc7c8510366147ca4e256b1a1f3896717f4c50d4)

`leptoskit_aria::Tabs` is now one stop for the Tab key. Only the selected tab is in the Tab order; Left and Right (Up and Down after `.orientation(Orientation::Vertical)`), Home and End move to another tab, select it, and take focus with it.

**Breaking:** the selection callback moved from each tab to the list. Write `tabs.list(move |index| …)` and `tabs.tab(index, label)` where you wrote `tabs.list()` and `tabs.tab(index, label, move |index| …)`. `Tabs` no longer implements `PartialEq`.

`leptoskit_aria::RadioGroup` is new: a choice of one option among several where each option shows any content, such as a card. `RadioGroup::new(id, labels, selected).option(index, content).on_change(…)` becomes an element with `Element::from`. Options carry the `radio` role, their checked state and their position; the group is one Tab stop, and the arrow keys, Home and End move, choose and take focus along.

The arrow keys work on the web and in the terminal. macOS, iOS, Android, Windows and GTK do not deliver key presses to the app yet, so every tab and option stays reachable with Tab there, as before.

`leptoskit_testing::WidgetTester::press_key(finder, key)` presses a key on a widget and bubbles it to the nearest `on_key` handler.

#### Scroll an element into view with `Reveal`

_Owner:_ Ifiok Jr. · _Introduced in:_ [6aef48a](https://github.com/leptoskit/leptoskit/commit/6aef48a580ac38f8dc06b281c49c9036faf04151)

A screen can now bring one element into view without knowing where layout put it. Create a `Reveal`, give it to the element with `reveal_on(&reveal, ScrollAlign::Nearest)`, and call `reveal.request()` from any handler. Each request scrolls once, after the next update, and the person scrolls freely afterwards. `ScrollAlign` is `Start`, `Center`, `End` or `Nearest`, and `Nearest` does nothing when the element is already in view.

On the web this is the browser's `scrollIntoView`, smooth unless the person asked for reduced motion. In native apps the surface works out the offset from layout and scrolls the nearest `ScrollView` around the element. Only that one view scrolls, and an element outside any `ScrollView` is left alone.

The GTK, Windows, AppKit and UIKit backend crates now apply `scroll_offset`, which they ignored before, so `Reveal` and `VirtualList`'s programmatic scrolling work in the generated Windows and Linux apps. GTK, Windows and AppKit jump to the offset; UIKit animates when asked. The terminal and HarmonyOS still don't scroll from code.

`NativeProps` gains a `reveal` field, which the surface answers itself and never sends to a backend.

#### Service workers and stronger extension messaging

_Owner:_ Ifiok Jr. · _Introduced in:_ [363ebad](https://github.com/leptoskit/leptoskit/commit/363ebadd2effe51d9b954c31ab0b6bcbfdc46ab8)

Web apps can enable the `service-worker` feature to register a worker script, exchange messages, describe caching strategies, open Cache Storage, and manage Web Push subscriptions. Calls return `Unavailable` outside a secure browser context.

Browser extensions gain long-lived `runtime::connect` ports (with `Background::on_connect`), storage `clear` / `keys` / `get_bytes_in_use`, and permissions `get_all` / `on_added` / `on_removed`. The generated background worker keeps ports alive so the wasm side can post and disconnect by id.

#### Serve streams from a server that has no database

_Owner:_ Ifiok Jr. · _Introduced in:_ [f7bf762](https://github.com/leptoskit/leptoskit/commit/f7bf762393787df34f5c07c85f9741e6cf6be5e9)

A `#[rpc::stream]` used to need the full live server, which reads a database's change log, so a service with something to stream and no database could not serve one.

- **`rpc::StreamCx`** is a new context for a stream's body. It holds who is calling (`get`, `require`, `signed_in`, `identity`) and no database. A stream that takes it runs on any live server. A stream that reads the database keeps `rpc::QueryCx`.
- **`rpc::server::LiveStreams`** serves streams alone, on the same routes as `Live` (the WebSocket, its server-sent events, and their frame posts) with the same limits. It takes `identify`, `origin`, `for_service`, `rpc_config`, `stall_timeout`, and `drain`. `Live::streams_only()` returns one too. A query, mutation, action, or channel sent to it is answered with a `501` that says why.
- **`live-streams`** is a new feature of `leptoskit_rpc` (`rpc-live-streams` through `leptoskit`). It needs no database driver and opens no connection. `live` now includes it.

Nothing changes for a client: `use_stream` reads either server.

Things to know when upgrading:

- A stream with no context argument no longer requires a database driver in the build. It needs `live-streams` or a driver, and `rpc::cx()` inside it works only where the server has a database.
- `StreamOperation::pump` and `StreamRegistration::open` now take the hidden `rpc::server::StreamOpen` in place of a `QueryCx`. Code generated by `#[rpc::stream]` follows by itself; a registration built by hand needs the new type.
- `LiveStreams` keeps an identity until its lease expires or the connection ends. It can't watch the rows a lease reads, because it has no change log.

#### TextArea: a field for several lines of text

_Owner:_ Ifiok Jr. · _Introduced in:_ [ce9d470](https://github.com/leptoskit/leptoskit/commit/ce9d470863cd327cdd87a36a12738c0fd356986c)

`TextArea()` is a new component, with its own `NativeKind::TextArea`, for notes, comments and messages. Enter adds a line instead of submitting, long lines wrap, and the field scrolls its own content. It is controlled like `TextInput`: `on_change` receives the proposed text with lines separated by `\n`, and `placeholder`, `read_only`, `max_length`, `capitalize`, `autocorrect` and `autocomplete` apply. It never raises `Submit`.

The web renders a `<textarea>`; macOS an `NSTextView` in an `NSScrollView`; iOS a `UITextView`; Android a multi-line `EditText`; Linux a `gtk::TextView` in a `gtk::ScrolledWindow`; Windows a multi-line `EDIT` control; the terminal a wrapping editor with line-wise arrow keys. The Swift and Kotlin renderers that generated apps use draw it too. GTK and Windows show no placeholder, and HarmonyOS and the watch surfaces do not draw the component.

`aria_multiline(true)` on a `TextInput` or `PasswordInput` now fails validation, because a single-line field that calls itself multi-line misreports itself to assistive technology. Use `TextArea` instead.

- **Typed text-input hints.** `TextInput` now carries the keyboard and text-editing hints that hand-written JavaScript used to provide, so every interface stays in leptoskit's own Wasm tree: `keyboard` (Text, Email, Number, Decimal, Phone, Url, Search), `read_only`, `max_length`, `capitalize` (None, Words, Sentences, Characters), `autocorrect`, and `submit_label` (Done, Go, Next, Search, Send). Each platform maps them to its own controls: the web to `type`, `inputmode`, `readonly`, `maxlength`, `autocapitalize`, `autocorrect`, `spellcheck`, and `enterkeyhint`; iOS to `keyboardType`, `autocapitalizationType`, `autocorrectionType`, `spellCheckingType`, and `returnKeyType`; Android to `inputType`, `imeOptions`, `InputFilter.LengthFilter`, and a cleared key listener for read-only fields; GTK to `set_input_purpose`, `set_editable`, `set_max_length`, and `InputHints`; macOS to `isEditable` and delegate truncation plus the field editor's correction and spell checking; Windows to `EM_SETREADONLY` and `EM_LIMITTEXT`. `read_only` implies `aria-readonly`. The Swift and Kotlin bridge renderers and the terminal backend honour the same props.
  _Owner:_ Ifiok Jr. · _Introduced in:_ [6d42b06](https://github.com/leptoskit/leptoskit/commit/6d42b068273560b572fa4c7f5f4475b33a03563b)

- **Ding-inspired toast pills.** Status toasts arrive as a 44px shape, spring open into a pill, morph in place when a newer message arrives, and shrink before they leave — the same phase model and spring tunings as [Ding](https://github.com/YusufCeng1z/ding). Hold a `Toaster`, call `success` / `error` / `warning` / `info` / `loading`, rebuild from `toaster.state()`, and advance phases with `poll`. `ToastViewport` draws the stack from shared builders, so every backend that already draws `View`, `Text`, `Button`, and `Vector` can show a toast.
  _Owner:_ Ifiok Jr. · _Introduced in:_ [ab77e98](https://github.com/leptoskit/leptoskit/commit/ab77e9807ae2c781c3d7a80ff5e00c270cfac4b6)

#### Add `use_clock`, a clock that advances by itself

_Owner:_ Ifiok Jr. · _Introduced in:_ [95d9169](https://github.com/leptoskit/leptoskit/commit/95d9169b4306a60430916d2d39ab8d4f4afe6785)

`leptoskit_use::use_clock(interval)` returns a `Clock` signal holding the time since it was called, updated about once per `interval` on the platform's own timer: `setTimeout` in the browser, the timer plugin in a native app, and tokio or a timer thread elsewhere. Pass it to `use_timeout_fn`, `use_interval_fn`, `signal_debounced` and the other hooks that take a clock, or read it in a `Text` closure for a countdown. Until now a host had to advance a clock signal itself.

The time is measured from the wall clock and never goes back, so a tab that slept catches up in one step. The timer stops when the owner the clock was made under is cleaned up.

It is behind a new `clock` feature, because it is the one hook in `leptoskit_use` that needs a task executor and depends on `leptoskit_query`. In `leptoskit`, the `clock` feature turns on `use` and `query` too.

sections.title: Fixes
entries:
- **Over the air updates get their own section.** The home page and README now lead with one component tree and real native widgets. Over-the-air updates have their own section, describing code push for installed native apps and which generated hosts install releases.
  _Owner:_ Ifiok Jr. · _Introduced in:_ [8a98548](https://github.com/leptoskit/leptoskit/commit/8a98548690f1654a63c9b6adffe8b603ba3bbfb5)

#### Check independent consumers before crate publication

_Owner:_ Ifiok Jr. · _Introduced in:_ [b6a1990](https://github.com/leptoskit/leptoskit/commit/b6a1990a574a7c077e4f31d408550ae64045a016)

Compile eight separate browser, guest, server and auth feature combinations from the actual Cargo package payloads before publication. Require complete package resolution and reject server features in client builds. Retain per-consumer build logs and exact archive and lockfile hashes; failed or incomplete runs produce no successful acceptance report.

Reject archive paths and directory names that alias by case on every host, so Linux validation also catches archives that cannot extract on a case-insensitive filesystem.

Run validation during release dry runs without publisher credentials. Before upload, require freshly prepared archives to match the hashes from the successful consumer run on the same revision.

- **Fix the platform module guide's path from the source root.** The creating-an-app guide now uses `components/heading` for a module in `src/components/heading.rs`, matching `platform_module!`'s source-root-relative paths. The generated application's end-to-end test uses the same corrected declaration and still verifies adding and removing a platform override.
  _Owner:_ Ifiok Jr. · _Introduced in:_ [d9a66d1](https://github.com/leptoskit/leptoskit/commit/d9a66d1e73141c14be24d3e57bcd4f1cf600bdca)

- **Add `leptoskit_plugin_background_task` for named OS background-task register/unregister/status/complete (`BGTaskScheduler` / `WorkManager`), distinct from `leptoskit_plugin_background` AppService keep-alive.** Guaranteed cadence and suspended Wasm execution remain later scope.
  _Owner:_ Ifiok Jr. · _Introduced in:_ [d5f4657](https://github.com/leptoskit/leptoskit/commit/d5f4657d76a38bde21d61af21eff755964a6ac13)

- **Add `leptoskit_plugin_calendar` for calendar permission, listing calendars (max 64), and creating or reading bounded events on iOS and Android.** Desktop and browser hosts report unavailable.
  _Owner:_ Ifiok Jr. · _Introduced in:_ [7b07d8f](https://github.com/leptoskit/leptoskit/commit/7b07d8f5999a34ede92c671fbe1c524dd49b7313)

- **Add `leptoskit_plugin_contacts` for contacts permission, system pick-one, and a bounded query (max 32) on iOS and Android.** Desktop and browser hosts report unavailable.
  _Owner:_ Ifiok Jr. · _Introduced in:_ [3820e86](https://github.com/leptoskit/leptoskit/commit/3820e86dfca1283e2ed1f36e4a34befdfc03a564)

- **Add `leptoskit_plugin_device_motion` for fused attitude, user acceleration, and rotation-rate readings on iOS, Android, and the browser.** Desktop hosts report unavailable.
  _Owner:_ Ifiok Jr. · _Introduced in:_ [dda0a88](https://github.com/leptoskit/leptoskit/commit/dda0a88a43b312383c51c7b0c1f46cdad7005e05)

- **Add `leptoskit_plugin_live_photo` with create/start/stop/status/release and a `LivePhoto` surface bound by session id (`PHLivePhotoView`).** Android and browser remain Unavailable; editing remains later scope.
  _Owner:_ Ifiok Jr. · _Introduced in:_ [13da9d6](https://github.com/leptoskit/leptoskit/commit/13da9d61f3252c056816f1da31516fd4e5040f9c)

- **Add `leptoskit_plugin_maps` with create/camera/markers/status/release and a `Map` surface bound by session id (MapKit / Google Maps).** User location and shapes remain later scope.
  _Owner:_ Ifiok Jr. · _Introduced in:_ [10ddb6f](https://github.com/leptoskit/leptoskit/commit/10ddb6fef86dc107d73054a9e2f2542f6e922da8)

- **Add `leptoskit_plugin_media_library` for bounded photo-library permission, asset listing, and saving an app-owned file into the system library.** Change observation remains later scope.
  _Owner:_ Ifiok Jr. · _Introduced in:_ [5e5b6cd](https://github.com/leptoskit/leptoskit/commit/5e5b6cd704fae36b0331982beb725e9a61d1a1e5)

#### Keep focus across web rebuilds and inside modals

_Owner:_ Ifiok Jr. · _Introduced in:_ [a1dd169](https://github.com/leptoskit/leptoskit/commit/a1dd169266d9fc0c2bc17705cdcc0afe846fb584)

On the web, a screen that rebuilt replaced every landmark (`main`, `nav`, `header`, `footer`, `aside`, `article`, `section`, `search`), every heading, list, paragraph and label with a new element, instead of updating the one already there. Anything inside went with it: a text field lost its focus and its selection, and a person typing was dropped back to the top of the page.

Those elements now update in place, as `div` and `span` always did, so focus stays where it was after any rebuild.

A rebuild also no longer takes a node's `id`, `role`, `aria-*` and `tabindex` attributes off and puts them back: it sets the ones whose value changed and removes the ones that are gone. Before, a focused element that is only focusable through `tabindex`, such as a dialog's heading, lost focus to the page on every rebuild.

A `Modal` on the web now wraps Tab: past its last control focus comes back to its first, and Shift+Tab past its first goes to its last, instead of leaving the page for the browser's toolbar.

#### Keyboard shortcuts for the whole app on the web

_Owner:_ Ifiok Jr. · _Introduced in:_ [8de3f4c](https://github.com/leptoskit/leptoskit/commit/8de3f4c497639561553ce1d2767baabbe41f2933)

`use_shortcut` runs a function when the person presses a key, wherever focus is, even when nothing has focus. It suits ⌘K to search or a single letter that opens a drawer, which `on_key` can't express because it only hears keys pressed inside its element.

```rust
let search = FocusRequest::new();
use_shortcut(Shortcut::primary("k"), move || search.request());
use_shortcut(Shortcut::key("w").unless_typing(), move || toggle_drawer());
```

`Shortcut::primary` holds ⌘ on Apple devices and Ctrl elsewhere. `.shift()` and `.alt()` add modifiers, and `.unless_typing()` leaves the key alone in a text field. A shortcut stops when its component goes, the newest of two matching shortcuts wins, and a key an element's `on_key` handled never reaches one.

Shortcuts work on the web today. Native hosts and the terminal don't deliver keys to them yet, so there a shortcut does nothing for now.

_Owner:_ Ifiok Jr. · _Introduced in:_ [f25ea8c](https://github.com/leptoskit/leptoskit/commit/f25ea8c94f5875355ce081afae5ac92a652cee48)

The value reaches the provider's authorization page as OpenID Connect's `prompt` parameter, and a provider that doesn't know the parameter ignores it.

```rust
Pressable("Open the admin")
	.href("https://admin.example.com/")
	.target(LinkTarget::NewTab)
	.child(Text("Open the admin ↗"));

```

Native apps used to ignore `href`. With the new `links` feature, pressing a link that has no `on_press` handler opens an absolute HTTP(S), `mailto:`, `tel:` or `sms:` link outside the app, through `leptoskit_plugin_linking`: directly on macOS, Windows and Linux, and through the host's `linking` plugin in a Wasm guest on iOS and Android. The app's server describes people with `set_person_attributes` (batch, ≤1,000 people, idempotent; keys `a-z0-9_` ≤64 bytes, values ≤256 bytes, ≤50 attributes per person with cap-skipping counted; `person_attributes` reads back; `forget_person` removes the person from the registry with their attributes and topic subscriptions, keeping their inbox) — app-only by design, so a segment can't be forged from the client side. SQLite and Postgres migrations add `persons` and `person_attributes` with the registry backfill.
