The `leptoskit_cloud_app` server reads `LEPTOSKIT_CLOUD_STRIPE_KEY`, `LEPTOSKIT_CLOUD_STRIPE_WEBHOOK_SECRET`, `LEPTOSKIT_CLOUD_STRIPE_PRICES`, `LEPTOSKIT_CLOUD_STRIPE_AUTOMATIC_TAX` and `LEPTOSKIT_CLOUD_STRIPE_TEST_MODE`; a Stripe test key is refused outside `--dev` without the last. A plan that is sold needs a `monthly` price and a `spend_cap` in the catalogue, and `set_spend_cap` now refuses a cap above the plan's own (`cap_above_plan`). Usage beyond what a plan includes is still not invoiced.

- **The groundwork for LeptosKit Cloud.** `leptoskit.toml` accepts a `[cloud]` table that says where LeptosKit Cloud should run your app and how big: a project, an optional region, and per-environment size, replicas, sleeping when idle and custom domains, plus the database's size and backups. Config checks it as it loads, with errors that name the table and key, such as a SQLite app asking for more than one replica, or sleeping while it serves live queries. The new `leptoskit_cloud` crate holds the shared types behind it: slugs, sizes, deployment states, the source archive a deploy will upload (deterministic, with secret files refused), and a monthly cost estimate for a `[cloud]` table. The cloud itself doesn't run yet, so nothing deploys there today.
  _Owner:_ Ifiok Jr. · _Introduced in:_ [403aaf0](https://github.com/leptoskit/leptoskit/commit/403aaf07e6df872150ffa904a48c1a9d55e1b6ed)
#### Cloud serves notifications from a shared hub

_Owner:_ Ifiok Jr. · _Introduced in:_ [78c0bf4](https://github.com/leptoskit/leptoskit/commit/78c0bf47afd1e2e6c741d5d3cb79f0692ef0b985)

An app that declares `[services.notifications]` with `crate = "leptoskit_notifications"` runs no process for it in LeptosKit Cloud. Its environment becomes a tenant of its cluster's notifications hub, a worker of the new role `notifications`:

- `lk cloud deploy` reports the service as `hosted = "notifications"`, with whether the app forwards identity. The build worker builds nothing for it.
- A deployment makes the tenant once: a database of its own, `ntf_` and the environment's ID, on the cluster's Postgres server, and a token the app and the hub share, both sealed in the vault. A cluster without a hub or a Postgres server refuses the deployment as `notifications_unavailable`.
- The release bridges to the hub as a platform service, routes `/_leptoskit/services/notifications/` on every hostname to it when the service is public, and gives the app `LEPTOSKIT_SERVICE_NOTIFICATIONS_URL`, `_IDENTITY` and, leased with the release, `_TOKEN`. The cluster's worker is leased the database's address as `LEPTOSKIT_NOTIFICATIONS_DATABASE_URL`.
- Push credentials and settings are the service's own `LEPTOSKIT_NOTIFICATIONS_*` names, set as secrets or variables. They are exempt from the reserved prefix, never given to the app's processes, and changing one reloads the tenant on the hub without a deployment.
- The hub asks for its cluster's tenants with `notification_tenants`, is given each changed one's values (recorded in `notification_leases` first), and reports how each is doing and how many pushes each sent with `report_notifications`. Pushes are the new meter `notification_pushes`.
- `notifications` tells anyone who can view the project the tenant's state, which providers have settings, and the project's pushes this month.

#### A free plan's hosted pushes stop at its monthly allowance

_Owner:_ Ifiok Jr. · _Introduced in:_ [3d2887b](https://github.com/leptoskit/leptoskit/commit/3d2887b72737ef9972a8374a5a6d79b24500ff5a)

When an organisation on a plan that costs nothing has used its plan's `notification_pushes` allowance for the month, LeptosKit Cloud stops its hosted notifications from sending pushes until the next month or until it moves to a paid plan. The inbox, live updates and every other operation keep working, and `lk cloud notifications` says `Pushes are paused`. The pushes a service sends before it hears are free up to the allowance again, so they don't reach the free plan's spend cap and stop deploys; past twice the allowance they are priced and reach it, as before. A free plan that lists no `notification_pushes` allowance is billed as before. The price itself is the operator's catalogue: for example 10,000 pushes a month on every plan, then 10 cents per 1,000 on paid plans.

The control plane's `notification_tenants` answer gains `paused`, the cluster's tenants whose pushes are stopped, and the `notifications` summary gains `pushes_paused`; both default to empty and `false`. The hub stops and starts each tenant's pushes on its answer without reopening it.

`leptoskit_notifications` gains `service::push::Paused`, a switch on `service::push::Push` that a server's runner can flip while it runs. While it is on, each push is skipped with the new delivery reason `paused`, and `send_test` is refused with a `400`. Code that builds `Push` by hand adds `paused: Paused::default()`.

#### Rotate notifications credentials when a worker is revoked

_Owner:_ Ifiok Jr. · _Introduced in:_ [188e2b9](https://github.com/leptoskit/leptoskit/commit/188e2b93aa068084af3ef2791751026d83ee9465)

Revoking a cluster's worker or its notifications hub now gives every hosted notifications tenant on that cluster a new database password and token. The next deployment applies them: until then, the hub accepts the old and the new values, and the `notifications` summary reports `rotating`.

`ServiceCallers::forwarded_identity` can now be called more than once, so a service accepts people forwarded with either token while its token is being replaced.

When the cluster's worker sets a notifications tenant's database password, it now ends that role's other sessions, so a connection made with the old password doesn't outlive it. Its Postgres administrator needs superuser access or the `pg_signal_backend` role.

- **Store publishing needs the `publish` token scope.** An API token with only the `deploy` scope can no longer publish to the app and extension stores. Publishing has its own permission now, which owners, admins and developers hold and which only the `publish` scope grants to a token, so that scope now lets a token publish where before it granted nothing but reading. A CI job that runs `lk cloud publish` needs both scopes, because the command uploads the source archive before it queues the publish: `lk cloud token create ci --scope deploy --scope publish`. A token with `deploy` alone is refused by `publish` with `403 insufficient_scope`. Reading a publish, its report and its log is unchanged.
  _Owner:_ Ifiok Jr. · _Introduced in:_ [b2f38fb](https://github.com/leptoskit/leptoskit/commit/b2f38fb0e3ffb4aad87342a3576b2e5abfc1efd8)
#### Publish to app and extension stores from the cloud

_Owner:_ Ifiok Jr. · _Introduced in:_ [101b2ee](https://github.com/leptoskit/leptoskit/commit/101b2ee1e7acf5a060554a6a0bd7c9f597ff7903)

`leptoskit_cloud::publishing` adds `publish`, which builds an uploaded archive for its stores and uploads it on one of the organisation's build workers, as `lk publish` does, with the environment's secrets named as `lk publish` reads them. `publication`, `publications` and `publication_log` read a publish back, with its report and its log. A publish is never run twice, since it may have reached a store. `JobKind`, `JobInput` and `JobOutcome` gain `Publish`; store credentials may now be set as secrets, and no release is given them.

`leptoskit publish` takes a keystore's `_BASE64` variable in place of its path for Google Play and the Solana dApp Store, and with `LEPTOSKIT_PUBLISH_CONTENTS_ONLY=1` refuses a credential that names a file.

### Fixes

- **Build logs are charged what they keep, and bounded in chunks.** A build's log is charged to the build's cap (`ShippingSettings::build_log_cap`) and to its organisation's (`organization_log_cap`) as its chunks are stored, not as the worker sent their lines. A chunk of blank lines used to be kept and charged nothing, so neither cap ever engaged; it now counts like any other. A job's log also has at most `MAX_BUILD_LOG_CHUNKS` (4,096) chunks over all its attempts, whatever their bytes, and a chunk past that is refused with `409 log_full`.
  _Owner:_ Ifiok Jr. · _Introduced in:_ [0696997](https://github.com/leptoskit/leptoskit/commit/0696997b3d6d4e549e19a8e2b21713da4dbde9f6)
- **Hold a build's reported steps to a bound.** A build worker's report is held to at most 200 steps, whatever it sent. Each step becomes an event of its deployment's and goes on its sheet, and one report could carry as many steps as its output file fits. Past the bound the last step kept says how many were left out, and a step's name is kept to 500 bytes. A report within the bound is kept as it was sent.
  _Owner:_ Ifiok Jr. · _Introduced in:_ [81054a0](https://github.com/leptoskit/leptoskit/commit/81054a09cf174adcc8509131104b170f42054055)
- **Hold an organisation's own spend cap to its plan's cap.** An organisation's own spend cap could only be set up to the cap of the plan it was on at the time. When the organisation later moved to a plan with a lower cap, its own cap stayed as it was, so usage was allowed past the new plan's cap. Now, when a plan change moves an organisation to a plan whose cap is lower than its own cap, the own cap comes down to that plan's cap. An own cap that already fits is left as it is, whichever way the organisation moves.
  _Owner:_ Ifiok Jr. · _Introduced in:_ [ee00cca](https://github.com/leptoskit/leptoskit/commit/ee00cca1030469e08f62ffb4449d4ad503c052c8)
#### Close the control plane's second security review

_Owner:_ Ifiok Jr. · _Introduced in:_ [dedf032](https://github.com/leptoskit/leptoskit/commit/dedf032eb758ec35adc6689619328df598e6c427)

An upload keeps the size it was begun with, and each archive has its own object key, so no ticket uploads more than the storage cap counted and a swept archive never takes a later upload with it. `claim` filters by role, organisation and cluster and pages through the queue, so one cluster's or organisation's backlog no longer starves the rest.

A build's log, an organisation's build logs, and the time one attempt at a build may run are all capped (`ShippingSettings::build_log_cap`, `organization_log_cap`, `build_deadline`). A build's lease past its end no longer renews, logs, or finishes. A build can only name images in the repository its job was given. `rollback` is refused while the database's migrations are uncertain. A removal that failed stays in front of operators, with its reason in `JobSummary::failure`, until it is reconciled or its worker reports it done. A status report's lines are stored in chunks small enough to read back.

Log lines hide a secret split over a chunk's lines, and write control characters out instead of passing them to a reader's terminal.

- **Invitation mail to one address is limited to five an hour.** Inviting an address again mailed it again and replaced its earlier invitation, so the cap on pending invitations never grew: anyone who could invite could send one address any amount of mail from the platform's sender. An organisation may now send five invitations to one address in an hour. After that, `invite_member` answers `rate_limited` until one of that hour's invitations is an hour old, and changes nothing; other addresses aren't held up. The limit is for each organisation on its own: several organisations can still each send five.
  _Owner:_ Ifiok Jr. · _Introduced in:_ [2ae5db1](https://github.com/leptoskit/leptoskit/commit/2ae5db1aa020157c4fced7ce54d39c325412e116)
- **Promote the bootstrap operator once per database.** With `LEPTOSKIT_CLOUD_BOOTSTRAP_OPERATOR_EMAIL` set, `leptoskit-cloud-control` makes that address an operator while the database has never had one. Before, it did so again at every start or `migrate` that found no operator, so revoking that address was undone by the next start. The promotion now stops once the audit log holds an `operator.bootstrap` or `operator.grant` entry, so `operator revoke` stays final. `operator revoke` says so when it removes the configured address and no operator remains.
  _Owner:_ Ifiok Jr. · _Introduced in:_ [a53a454](https://github.com/leptoskit/leptoskit/commit/a53a4542f7ffd915ae725ede071581ebb9891300)
#### A platform hostname is held until its removal is reported

_Owner:_ Ifiok Jr. · _Introduced in:_ [5debb82](https://github.com/leptoskit/leptoskit/commit/5debb829cfe5edc864b81d75c29f6d5b5dd62c97)

Deleting an environment, or the project that holds it, used to free its platform hostname at once, while the cluster could still serve it until its worker finished the removal. Another organisation could take the hostname in that window and be served at it to the environment's former visitors. A placement now outlives its environment, marked `removing`, and keeps the hostname until the cluster's worker reports the removal done or an operator settles it. A placement being removed isn't counted as an environment its cluster runs, so it doesn't send new work to that cluster.

The `placement_claims` migration (`20261125T222120_placement_claims` on SQLite, `20261125T222243_placement_claims` on Postgres) adds `environment_placements.removing`, `false` for every row a database already has, and removes the foreign key that deleted a placement with its environment. Its reverse restores that foreign key, so it fails while a removal is still pending.

- **Refuse `rollback` at the spend cap, as `deploy` is.** Once an organisation's usage for the month reaches its spend cap, `rollback` answers `spend_cap_reached` and makes no deployment, as `deploy` does. Until now a rollback could still put an earlier release live past the cap, and bring back a larger scale than the one running. What already runs keeps running: nothing is slept, stopped or deleted. Under the cap, rolling back works as before.
  _Owner:_ Ifiok Jr. · _Introduced in:_ [ef1837a](https://github.com/leptoskit/leptoskit/commit/ef1837a3eb2b7bd8d5672b5839912d68dd810837)
- **Keep control-plane tables and authentication dependencies behind the server feature so client types compile independently of database backend features.** Check isolated clients with no backend, SQLite, Postgres, both backends, and WebAssembly.
  _Owner:_ Ifiok Jr. · _Introduced in:_ [5e39638](https://github.com/leptoskit/leptoskit/commit/5e396387225c6d0f53e7762277214b6e54998208)
#### The control plane's sweeper runs with several replicas

_Owner:_ Ifiok Jr. · _Introduced in:_ [1dc5cd4](https://github.com/leptoskit/leptoskit/commit/1dc5cd4261a10990a6b1a49726698cca5f276ed6)

A control plane generated with two or more `[control_plane] replicas` was deployed with `LEPTOSKIT_CLOUD_SWEEPER=false`. A Deployment gives that value to every replica, so none of them ran the background sweeper: a worker's expired lease was not taken back, and expired archives and logs were not deleted. The generated manifest now sets the variable to `true` whatever the replica count. The sweeper already lets one replica sweep at a time with a Postgres advisory lock, and `LEPTOSKIT_CLOUD_SWEEPER=false` still switches it off.

The documentation of `LEPTOSKIT_CLOUD_SWEEPER` in `leptoskit_cloud_app` no longer says to set it to `false` on secondary replicas. The `run_sweeper` setting's documentation in `leptoskit_cloud` no longer tells operators to set it to `false` on secondary replicas.

- **Runtime logs hide the environment's own secrets.** A cluster's worker reports an environment's runtime logs to the control plane, which kept each line as the worker sent it. A process that printed one of the environment's secret values left it readable in the logs by anyone who could view the project. The control plane now opens the environment's current secrets as a report arrives and hides them from its lines and from a failed process's reason, from eight bytes up. A value shorter than that, or one the environment replaced or removed after the process started, is still kept as printed. A report is refused while a secret can't be opened, rather than kept as printed.
  _Owner:_ Ifiok Jr. · _Introduced in:_ [c3c3a55](https://github.com/leptoskit/leptoskit/commit/c3c3a553b9bc0fb69126dcdb22c1356cb2e13a9e)

sections.title: Features
entries:
#### Publish cloud CLI crates and prebuilt release binaries

_Owner:_ Ifiok Jr. · _Introduced in:_ [e47b3de](https://github.com/leptoskit/leptoskit/commit/e47b3de2192792651b71741c9094b14cf49492be)

- Registers `leptoskit_cloud_platform` (`leptoskit-cloud-platform`), `leptoskit_cloud_worker` (`leptoskit-cloud-worker`), and `leptoskit_cloud_app` (`leptoskit-cloud-control`) in `monochange.toml` and removes `publish = false` so all three crates version and publish with the main release group.
- Adds `[package.metadata.binstall]` to all three crates and extends `.github/workflows/publish.yml` to build, archive, upload, and provenance-attest prebuilt binaries for all release targets alongside `leptoskit` and `lk`.
- Bundles the console's two Latin font subsets inside `crates/leptoskit_cloud_app/assets/fonts/` so `leptoskit_cloud_app` packages cleanly for crates.io.
- Updates `lk cloud <name>` missing-binary hints to recommend `cargo binstall` and `cargo install`.

sections.title: Fixes
entries:
- **Promote the bootstrap operator once per database.** With `LEPTOSKIT_CLOUD_BOOTSTRAP_OPERATOR_EMAIL` set, `leptoskit-cloud-control` makes that address an operator while the database has never had one. Before, it did so again at every start or `migrate` that found no operator, so revoking that address was undone by the next start. The promotion now stops once the audit log holds an `operator.bootstrap` or `operator.grant` entry, so `operator revoke` stays final. `operator revoke` says so when it removes the configured address and no operator remains.
  _Owner:_ Ifiok Jr. · _Introduced in:_ [a53a454](https://github.com/leptoskit/leptoskit/commit/a53a4542f7ffd915ae725ede071581ebb9891300)

#### Console pages can't be framed by another site

_Owner:_ Ifiok Jr. · _Introduced in:_ [81054a0](https://github.com/leptoskit/leptoskit/commit/81054a09cf174adcc8509131104b170f42054055)

The console sent no `frame-ancestors` policy with its pages, so a site on the console's own domain could show a console page inside a frame. Tenant apps are served on the apps domain, and nothing keeps that domain off the console's site: the example configurations put both on `example.com`. A browser then sends the console's session cookie to the framed page, and one click inside the frame approves a terminal on `/device`, signs out a device on `/account`, or resets an organisation's spend cap.

Every page the console answers with now carries `Content-Security-Policy: frame-ancestors 'none'`, with `X-Content-Type-Options: nosniff` and `Referrer-Policy: no-referrer`, so a browser refuses to draw the page in a frame. The pages the control plane answers itself, which the console's own middleware never sees, get `frame-ancestors 'none'` too, added to a policy the page already sets.

#### The control plane's sweeper runs with several replicas

_Owner:_ Ifiok Jr. · _Introduced in:_ [1dc5cd4](https://github.com/leptoskit/leptoskit/commit/1dc5cd4261a10990a6b1a49726698cca5f276ed6)

A control plane generated with two or more `[control_plane] replicas` was deployed with `LEPTOSKIT_CLOUD_SWEEPER=false`. A Deployment gives that value to every replica, so none of them ran the background sweeper: a worker's expired lease was not taken back, and expired archives and logs were not deleted. The generated manifest now sets the variable to `true` whatever the replica count. The sweeper already lets one replica sweep at a time with a Postgres advisory lock, and `LEPTOSKIT_CLOUD_SWEEPER=false` still switches it off.

The documentation of `LEPTOSKIT_CLOUD_SWEEPER` in `leptoskit_cloud_app` no longer says to set it to `false` on secondary replicas. The `run_sweeper` setting's documentation in `leptoskit_cloud` no longer tells operators to set it to `false` on secondary replicas.

sections.title: Features
entries:
#### Add the cloud notifications hub

_Owner:_ Ifiok Jr. · _Introduced in:_ [abe023c](https://github.com/leptoskit/leptoskit/commit/abe023cd7fd875aff9cb3098439359bed61bd26e)

`leptoskit-cloud-notifications` serves the hosted notifications of every environment on one cluster. It runs from a worker paired for the `notifications` role. Each round, it asks the control plane which tenants changed, and opens each tenant's database, migrated, with that tenant's token and push settings. It drops the tenants it is told to, and reports how each tenant is doing and how many pushes each one's providers accepted.

The hub serves a tenant's `/_leptoskit/services/notifications/` routes in two ways: by the tenant's hostname, for the edge, and under `/t/<tenant>/`, for the app's own calls.

The worker's control-plane client gains `notification_tenants` and `report_notifications`.

The notifications service keeps a ledger of accepted pushes, `push_acceptances`, written with each acceptance. It names no person, so `forget_person` and retention leave it, and the retention sweep deletes its rows after 90 days. A host that meters pushes counts it. Run the new migration before deploying. The service's settings wrapper now passes the callers' socket leases and limits through, so a lease the app's callers set expires a socket as it does without settings.

#### Run the notifications hub on platform clusters

_Owner:_ Ifiok Jr. · _Introduced in:_ [d4f1c23](https://github.com/leptoskit/leptoskit/commit/d4f1c236b3130b7c7a9266215fc44b66fdc4054a)

`[workers] notifications_image` makes `leptoskit-cloud-platform` run each cluster's notifications hub: the `leptoskit-notifications` namespace with `Deployment/hub` and `Service/hub` on port 8080, a policy that admits the apps' namespaces on that port only, and the cluster worker told where the hub is.

The hub pairs itself from `LEPTOSKIT_CLOUD_NOTIFICATIONS_PAIRING_CODE` with `--url` and `--name` while its state isn't paired. Its image, `leptoskit-cloud-notifications`, is built from the worker's Dockerfile, and its binary ships with each release.

#### A free plan's hosted pushes stop at its monthly allowance

_Owner:_ Ifiok Jr. · _Introduced in:_ [3d2887b](https://github.com/leptoskit/leptoskit/commit/3d2887b72737ef9972a8374a5a6d79b24500ff5a)

When an organisation on a plan that costs nothing has used its plan's `notification_pushes` allowance for the month, LeptosKit Cloud stops its hosted notifications from sending pushes until the next month or until it moves to a paid plan. The inbox, live updates and every other operation keep working, and `lk cloud notifications` says `Pushes are paused`. The pushes a service sends before it hears are free up to the allowance again, so they don't reach the free plan's spend cap and stop deploys; past twice the allowance they are priced and reach it, as before. A free plan that lists no `notification_pushes` allowance is billed as before. The price itself is the operator's catalogue: for example 10,000 pushes a month on every plan, then 10 cents per 1,000 on paid plans.

The control plane's `notification_tenants` answer gains `paused`, the cluster's tenants whose pushes are stopped, and the `notifications` summary gains `pushes_paused`; both default to empty and `false`. The hub stops and starts each tenant's pushes on its answer without reopening it.

`leptoskit_notifications` gains `service::push::Paused`, a switch on `service::push::Push` that a server's runner can flip while it runs. While it is on, each push is skipped with the new delivery reason `paused`, and `send_test` is refused with a `400`. Code that builds `Push` by hand adds `paused: Paused::default()`.

#### Rotate notifications credentials when a worker is revoked

_Owner:_ Ifiok Jr. · _Introduced in:_ [188e2b9](https://github.com/leptoskit/leptoskit/commit/188e2b93aa068084af3ef2791751026d83ee9465)

Revoking a cluster's worker or its notifications hub now gives every hosted notifications tenant on that cluster a new database password and token. The next deployment applies them: until then, the hub accepts the old and the new values, and the `notifications` summary reports `rotating`.

`ServiceCallers::forwarded_identity` can now be called more than once, so a service accepts people forwarded with either token while its token is being replaced.

When the cluster's worker sets a notifications tenant's database password, it now ends that role's other sessions, so a connection made with the old password doesn't outlive it. Its Postgres administrator needs superuser access or the `pg_signal_backend` role.

sections.title: Features
entries:
#### Harden cloud manifests and fix Day-1 platform blockers

_Owner:_ Ifiok Jr. · _Introduced in:_ [29e916b](https://github.com/leptoskit/leptoskit/commit/29e916be038faad465ec62d3fc0e0dff905cfd56)

`ClusterProfile` gains `Serialize`/`Deserialize`, `edge_terminated_custom_domains` (for Cloudflare for SaaS custom domains without cert-manager annotations), `tenant_node_selector` and `tenant_tolerations` (to isolate tenant pods onto dedicated tenant pools), and `tmp_size_limit_mib` (bounding `/tmp` `emptyDir` and container/namespace `ephemeral-storage`). `worker_admission_policy` emits a `ValidatingAdmissionPolicy` restricting cluster-worker mutations to `lk-*` tenant namespaces.

The platform generator fixes CloudNativePG superuser access, `max_connections` (300), and `pg_hba`; renames the KEDA HTTP `HelmChart` to `keda-add-ons-http`; re-enables `metrics-server` and kubelet metrics scraping for CPU HPAs; adds k3s `secrets-encryption`; fixes Cloudflare Tunnel catch-all routing for custom domains and adds an `apps-http01` HTTP-01 `ClusterIssuer` for `cert-manager` mode; keeps Zot cluster-local by default; hardens `cloudflared` and `platform-ingress` allowlist policies; allows ICMP in `nftables`; supports per-node `isolation_platform` overrides and hot/cold S3 backup splits; and fixes hybrid `growth.toml` disk sizing and `advertise-address`.

- **Apply tenant releases through Kubernetes with bounded rollout waits, observed status, logs, safe pruning and namespace deletion.** Align sleep routing and cluster profiles with the platform add-ons and generate the worker's permissions.
  _Owner:_ Ifiok Jr. · _Introduced in:_ [ce06091](https://github.com/leptoskit/leptoskit/commit/ce06091df4bfe19985bb279678f2776aea1744dd)

- **LeptosKit Cloud's runtime crate: a release as data, and the Kubernetes objects that carry it.** `ReleaseSpec` is the whole desired state of one environment — the app and its services with exact image digests, ports, health paths, environment and secret variables, resources, scale, and volumes; the routes; and the policy — with typed validation that refuses a spec no runtime could honor, and a namespace hashed from the organisation, project, and environment ids so no customer-chosen name ever reaches Kubernetes. The `Runtime` trait is the adapter boundary (`apply`, `status`, `logs`, `destroy`), usable as `dyn Runtime`, with a recording fake behind the `testing` feature that validates specs and scripts ready, never-ready, and unavailable rollouts. The `kubernetes` feature builds the release's manifests deterministically: the namespace under the restricted Pod Security profile, quota and limit range, default-deny network policies with the release's doors only, a token-less service account, hardened Deployments, Services, KEDA's HTTP scaled object or a horizontal autoscaler, disruption budgets, and Ingresses with wildcard or cert-manager certificates — refusing, before anything is applied, sleep without the HTTP add-on, cookie stripping a plain Ingress cannot do, a secret with no value, and an issued certificate with no issuer.
  _Owner:_ Ifiok Jr. · _Introduced in:_ [a66ec54](https://github.com/leptoskit/leptoskit/commit/a66ec5415deb156d6ac5e38f2c3aa29c4e172003)

- **A release can route to a service the platform runs.** `ReleaseSpec.platform` names services the platform runs outside the environment, such as its cluster's shared notifications hub. A route may name one instead of a process. The manifests give each a bridge in the environment's namespace, an `ExternalName` Service with the service's port, route to it, and open the namespace's egress to that service's namespace on that port and nothing more of it. A spec without platform services serializes as before, and one written before they existed reads with none.
  _Owner:_ Ifiok Jr. · _Introduced in:_ [8af1a5d](https://github.com/leptoskit/leptoskit/commit/8af1a5d4bf541ce8291c93badfa7bc5e179be046)

- **Reserve one surge pod for every process that rolls, and expose `Quota::for_processes` so control-plane quotas match runtime validation.** Processes with persistent volumes use Recreate and need no surge capacity.
  _Owner:_ Ifiok Jr. · _Introduced in:_ [ce06091](https://github.com/leptoskit/leptoskit/commit/ce06091df4bfe19985bb279678f2776aea1744dd)

### Features

#### Harden cloud manifests and fix Day-1 platform blockers

_Owner:_ Ifiok Jr. · _Introduced in:_ [29e916b](https://github.com/leptoskit/leptoskit/commit/29e916be038faad465ec62d3fc0e0dff905cfd56)

  _Owner:_ Ifiok Jr. · _Introduced in:_ [ce06091](https://github.com/leptoskit/leptoskit/commit/ce06091df4bfe19985bb279678f2776aea1744dd)
- **LeptosKit Cloud's runtime crate: a release as data, and the Kubernetes objects that carry it.** `ReleaseSpec` is the whole desired state of one environment — the app and its services with exact image digests, ports, health paths, environment and secret variables, resources, scale, and volumes; the routes; and the policy — with typed validation that refuses a spec no runtime could honor, and a namespace hashed from the organisation, project, and environment ids so no customer-chosen name ever reaches Kubernetes. The `Runtime` trait is the adapter boundary (`apply`, `status`, `logs`, `destroy`), usable as `dyn Runtime`, with a recording fake behind the `testing` feature that validates specs and scripts ready, never-ready, and unavailable rollouts.   _Owner:_ Ifiok Jr. · _Introduced in:_ [a66ec54](https://github.com/leptoskit/leptoskit/commit/a66ec5415deb156d6ac5e38f2c3aa29c4e172003)

#### Cluster worker makes notifications databases

_Owner:_ Ifiok Jr. · _Introduced in:_ [22c2e0e](https://github.com/leptoskit/leptoskit/commit/22c2e0e2a9fe938b58fe8cc9b66c1c0702a55d49)

A cluster's worker now makes sure of an environment's hosted notifications database, `ntf_` and the environment's ID, with each release that uses its cluster's notifications hub, and drops it with the environment. The database and its role are made and checked as an app's managed database is. The password, leased as `LEPTOSKIT_NOTIFICATIONS_DATABASE_URL`, is used by the worker alone and never given to the release's processes or written into a Secret.

A release bridged to a platform service is refused unless that service is the hub the new `--notifications-namespace`, `--notifications-host` and `--notifications-port` options name, exactly. Without them, every release that names a platform service is refused.

#### Publish cloud CLI crates and prebuilt release binaries

_Owner:_ Ifiok Jr. · _Introduced in:_ [e47b3de](https://github.com/leptoskit/leptoskit/commit/e47b3de2192792651b71741c9094b14cf49492be)

- Registers `leptoskit_cloud_platform` (`leptoskit-cloud-platform`), `leptoskit_cloud_worker` (`leptoskit-cloud-worker`), and `leptoskit_cloud_app` (`leptoskit-cloud-control`) in `monochange.toml` and removes `publish = false` so all three crates version and publish with the main release group.

entries:
#### Cloud serves notifications from a shared hub

_Owner:_ Ifiok Jr. · _Introduced in:_ [78c0bf4](https://github.com/leptoskit/leptoskit/commit/78c0bf47afd1e2e6c741d5d3cb79f0692ef0b985)

An app that declares `[services.notifications]` with `crate = "leptoskit_notifications"` runs no process for it in LeptosKit Cloud. Its environment becomes a tenant of its cluster's notifications hub, a worker of the new role `notifications`:

- `lk cloud deploy` reports the service as `hosted = "notifications"`, with whether the app forwards identity. The build worker builds nothing for it.
- A deployment makes the tenant once: a database of its own, `ntf_` and the environment's ID, on the cluster's Postgres server, and a token the app and the hub share, both sealed in the vault. A cluster without a hub or a Postgres server refuses the deployment as `notifications_unavailable`.
- The release bridges to the hub as a platform service, routes `/_leptoskit/services/notifications/` on every hostname to it when the service is public, and gives the app `LEPTOSKIT_SERVICE_NOTIFICATIONS_URL`, `_IDENTITY` and, leased with the release, `_TOKEN`. The cluster's worker is leased the database's address as `LEPTOSKIT_NOTIFICATIONS_DATABASE_URL`.
- Push credentials and settings are the service's own `LEPTOSKIT_NOTIFICATIONS_*` names, set as secrets or variables. They are exempt from the reserved prefix, never given to the app's processes, and changing one reloads the tenant on the hub without a deployment.
- The hub asks for its cluster's tenants with `notification_tenants`, is given each changed one's values (recorded in `notification_leases` first), and reports how each is doing and how many pushes each sent with `report_notifications`. Pushes are the new meter `notification_pushes`.
- `notifications` tells anyone who can view the project the tenant's state, which providers have settings, and the project's pushes this month.

#### Add the cloud notifications hub

_Owner:_ Ifiok Jr. · _Introduced in:_ [abe023c](https://github.com/leptoskit/leptoskit/commit/abe023cd7fd875aff9cb3098439359bed61bd26e)

`leptoskit-cloud-notifications` serves the hosted notifications of every environment on one cluster. It runs from a worker paired for the `notifications` role. Each round, it asks the control plane which tenants changed, and opens each tenant's database, migrated, with that tenant's token and push settings. It drops the tenants it is told to, and reports how each tenant is doing and how many pushes each one's providers accepted.

The hub serves a tenant's `/_leptoskit/services/notifications/` routes in two ways: by the tenant's hostname, for the edge, and under `/t/<tenant>/`, for the app's own calls.

The worker's control-plane client gains `notification_tenants` and `report_notifications`.

The notifications service keeps a ledger of accepted pushes, `push_acceptances`, written with each acceptance. It names no person, so `forget_person` and retention leave it, and the retention sweep deletes its rows after 90 days. A host that meters pushes counts it. Run the new migration before deploying. The service's settings wrapper now passes the callers' socket leases and limits through, so a lease the app's callers set expires a socket as it does without settings.

#### Run the notifications hub on platform clusters

_Owner:_ Ifiok Jr. · _Introduced in:_ [d4f1c23](https://github.com/leptoskit/leptoskit/commit/d4f1c236b3130b7c7a9266215fc44b66fdc4054a)

`[workers] notifications_image` makes `leptoskit-cloud-platform` run each cluster's notifications hub: the `leptoskit-notifications` namespace with `Deployment/hub` and `Service/hub` on port 8080, a policy that admits the apps' namespaces on that port only, and the cluster worker told where the hub is.

The hub pairs itself from `LEPTOSKIT_CLOUD_NOTIFICATIONS_PAIRING_CODE` with `--url` and `--name` while its state isn't paired. Its image, `leptoskit-cloud-notifications`, is built from the worker's Dockerfile, and its binary ships with each release.

#### Rotate notifications credentials when a worker is revoked

_Owner:_ Ifiok Jr. · _Introduced in:_ [188e2b9](https://github.com/leptoskit/leptoskit/commit/188e2b93aa068084af3ef2791751026d83ee9465)

Revoking a cluster's worker or its notifications hub now gives every hosted notifications tenant on that cluster a new database password and token. The next deployment applies them: until then, the hub accepts the old and the new values, and the `notifications` summary reports `rotating`.

`ServiceCallers::forwarded_identity` can now be called more than once, so a service accepts people forwarded with either token while its token is being replaced.

When the cluster's worker sets a notifications tenant's database password, it now ends that role's other sessions, so a connection made with the old password doesn't outlive it. Its Postgres administrator needs superuser access or the `pg_signal_backend` role.

#### A build worker's shared build cache is bounded

_Owner:_ Ifiok Jr. · _Introduced in:_ [e5fee56](https://github.com/leptoskit/leptoskit/commit/e5fee56762346d7604212ec733e30dcd273bca21)

A build worker keeps each project's build cache on one volume that every organisation whose builds run on the worker shares. Nothing capped a cache and nothing removed another project's, so one build with a large layer could fill the volume, and every organisation's next build then failed for want of space until someone deleted directories by hand.

Now a cache export larger than `--build-cache-max-mib` is removed once its build has succeeded. Before each build, the caches of other projects that no build has used for `--build-cache-idle-days` are removed, then the least recently used until no more than `--build-cache-max-used-percent` of the volume is taken. A build never removes the cache of the project it builds, and no build's result changes: a build whose cache was removed is only slower next time.

sections.title: Features
entries:
#### Versioned native capability contracts

_Owner:_ Ifiok Jr. · _Introduced in:_ [442b38b](https://github.com/leptoskit/leptoskit/commit/442b38b81352231ebb9810f646247bd548ed353c)

Native builds now resolve a typed host capability descriptor from the destination flavour, the plugin registrations they actually generated, and the non-secret plugin options. `native bundle` writes `capabilities.json` beside the bundle with a stable SHA-256 digest, and the mobile host embeds the same descriptor in `codepush.json`.

`[native]` gains `required-plugins`, `optional-plugins`, `required-capabilities`, and `optional-capabilities`. A required plugin or capability the selected host cannot run fails the build before packaging, regardless of `missing-plugins`; an optional omission warns with the platform and reason. Existing `plugins` and `missing-plugins` keep their behavior when no requirement lists are set, and a capability declaration never grants access.

Signed releases carry versioned required/optional requirements in `runtime.json`. The installed host checks them against its own descriptor before staging or activating an update; unsupported, unknown, or experimental-without-opt-in requirements are refused. Releases built before this format still pass the legacy ABI, shell, and plugin checks and are reported as legacy, never as verified-compatible. Unknown contract versions and conflicting or duplicate entries are rejected.

Guest requirements bind the bridge protocol as well as the rendering ABI. Explicitly optional plugins no longer enter the legacy required-plugin list. Watch preparation checks requirements before writing its stubs and emits a descriptor; standalone bundles place host evidence beside the output directory.

Updates whose older-style plugin grants have no available implementation report `incomplete` while preserving the existing missing-plugin fallback. Explicit required entries still reject unavailable plugins; explicit optional entries may be omitted. A versioned host descriptor must agree with its own grant list before it can check a release.

Generated iOS and Android update controls show whether host requirements were checked, plugin availability remains incomplete, or only legacy checks ran. A missing report from an older runtime is shown as unreported. None of these states claims that the updated app passed device tests.

The descriptor also names `host.timer` where the generated host enables the reserved `leptoskit.timer` plugin, so `required-capabilities = ["host.timer"]` fails before packaging on hosts that run no guest and is checked by code push on older store builds.

entries:
- **`[native.android] push` opts the Android app into FCM push enrollment.** It is a boolean, off by default: an app without it generates byte-for-byte as before. With it, Android generation adds the pinned `com.google.firebase:firebase-messaging` dependency, writes `.leptoskit/android/gradle-plugins.txt` with Google's services plugin, generates the messaging service that forwards FCM token refreshes to the notifications plugin, and declares that service in the manifest. Push on also requires the `notifications` plugin in `[native] plugins`, the app author's `google-services.json` at `hosts/android/app/google-services.json` — never generated or committed by leptoskit — and an app Gradle script that reads the generated plugins file (the current `leptoskit new` scaffold does; older apps get the exact lines from the generation error). The configuration schema carries the new key.
  _Owner:_ Ifiok Jr. · _Introduced in:_ [b782f13](https://github.com/leptoskit/leptoskit/commit/b782f1372a8b11ae1338a003c937282609188021)

#### Add cloud launch/deploy, storage config, and MCP tools

_Owner:_ Ifiok Jr. · _Introduced in:_ [94859ef](https://github.com/leptoskit/leptoskit/commit/94859efebd25f1bfb3f1c055c3172de4c309cad9)

- Adds `[cloud.storage.buckets.<name>]` configuration (`public`, `max_size_gb`) and updates the published `leptoskit.toml` JSON schemas.
- Adds `lk cloud launch`, `lk cloud deploy`, `lk cloud status`, `lk cloud logs [--follow]`, `lk cloud estimate`, and `lk cloud open`, wires `lk deploy` to dispatch to LeptosKit Cloud whenever `[cloud].project` is set, and adds Cargo-style external subcommand dispatch (`lk cloud <name>` → `leptoskit-cloud-<name>` on `PATH`, enabling `lk cloud platform`, `lk cloud worker`, and `lk cloud control`).
- Adds `--web-only` and `--cloud` flags to `lk new` and `lk generate app`, allows `--frontends` to combine with `--db`, `--auth`, `--web-only`, and `--cloud`, and falls back with a clear warning instead of hard-failing `lk dev` when `monosecret` is not installed.
- Exposes six cloud and database tools on `lk mcp` (`cloud_estimate`, `cloud_deploy`, `cloud_status`, `cloud_logs`, `cloud_secrets_list`, `db_check`) without ever returning secret values.

- **The groundwork for LeptosKit Cloud.** `leptoskit.toml` accepts a `[cloud]` table that says where LeptosKit Cloud should run your app and how big: a project, an optional region, and per-environment size, replicas, sleeping when idle and custom domains, plus the database's size and backups. Config checks it as it loads, with errors that name the table and key, such as a SQLite app asking for more than one replica, or sleeping while it serves live queries. The new `leptoskit_cloud` crate holds the shared types behind it: slugs, sizes, deployment states, the source archive a deploy will upload (deterministic, with secret files refused), and a monthly cost estimate for a `[cloud]` table. The cloud itself doesn't run yet, so nothing deploys there today.
  _Owner:_ Ifiok Jr. · _Introduced in:_ [403aaf0](https://github.com/leptoskit/leptoskit/commit/403aaf07e6df872150ffa904a48c1a9d55e1b6ed)

- **`[native.ios] aps-environment` names the APNs environment an iOS app opts into: `development` or `production`, exactly Apple's entitlement strings.** Unset by default.
  _Owner:_ Ifiok Jr. · _Introduced in:_ [b782f13](https://github.com/leptoskit/leptoskit/commit/b782f1372a8b11ae1338a003c937282609188021)

- **`[native.macos] aps-environment` names the APNs environment a macOS app opts into: `development` or `production`, exactly Apple's entitlement strings.** Unset by default.
  _Owner:_ Ifiok Jr. · _Introduced in:_ [b782f13](https://github.com/leptoskit/leptoskit/commit/b782f1372a8b11ae1338a003c937282609188021)

#### Add desktop window overlays and background modes

_Owner:_ Ifiok Jr. · _Introduced in:_ [9714421](https://github.com/leptoskit/leptoskit/commit/9714421722143255a82869b80b11b2b7be40f7ed)

- `leptoskit_plugin_window_state::desktop` adds Electron-class desktop windowing and lifecycle types: `WindowOptions` (with `floating_overlay` preset), `WindowLevel` (`Normal`, `Floating`, `AlwaysOnTop`, `Status`, `PopUpMenu`, `ScreenSaver`), `WindowChrome` (`Standard`, `Frameless`, `HiddenTitleBar`), `VibrancyMaterial` (macOS vibrancy and Windows Mica/Acrylic), `CloseBehavior` (`Quit`, `HideToTray`, `KeepRunningInBackground`, `Minimize`), `ActivationPolicy` (`Regular`, `Accessory`, `BackgroundOnly`), `TaskbarProgress`, `DockAttention`, `WindowController`, and `MemoryWindowController`.
- `leptoskit_config` adds `NativeMode::Background`, allows `menu-bar` and `background` startup modes across desktop platforms (`macos`, `windows`, `linux`), and adds the `[native.window]` configuration table (`DesktopWindowConfig`).

#### Add extension browser detection and full side panel API

_Owner:_ Ifiok Jr. · _Introduced in:_ [c4aa7df](https://github.com/leptoskit/leptoskit/commit/c4aa7df45dd07fbead27b9b05bba1d67ecfacd7f)

- `leptoskit_extension::browser` adds runtime browser detection (`ExtensionBrowser` covering Chrome, Edge, Brave, Opera, Arc, Vivaldi, Firefox, and Safari; `BrowserFamily`; `BrowserInfo`; `BrowserSwitch`; and `with_browser` test scoping).
- `leptoskit_extension::side_panel` adds full Chromium `chrome.sidePanel` and Firefox `browser.sidebarAction` support: `open_target`, `open_for_tab`, `close`, `toggle`, `is_open`, `set_options` / `get_options`, `set_behavior` / `get_behavior`, `get_layout`, `set_title` / `get_title`, and `capabilities`.
- Adds `leptoskit_extension::windows`, `leptoskit_extension::offscreen`, `leptoskit_extension::omnibox`, and `leptoskit_extension::native_messaging`.
- Adds `[extension].optional_permissions` and `[extension.side_panel]` `title` / `open_at_install` options to `leptoskit_config` and generated MV3 manifests.

- **JSON RPC wire and ambient context.** Queries and mutations speak JSON through serde on `POST /rpc/<name>`. `[rpc]` sets `path`, `live_path`, `transports`, and `default_transport`; the only transport is `json`. A query or mutation can omit its context argument and call `rpc::cx()` or `rpc::mutation_cx()`.
  _Owner:_ Ifiok Jr. · _Introduced in:_ [8bd1891](https://github.com/leptoskit/leptoskit/commit/8bd1891b8d987c9abe19128343e7107d706ecd88)

#### Meta Horizon Store publishing for Meta Quest

_Owner:_ Ifiok Jr. · _Introduced in:_ [f9e7c49](https://github.com/leptoskit/leptoskit/commit/f9e7c495e9fb4ef73cd8458d03b103a37083ff31)

Add `[publish.quest]` configuration and `leptoskit publish quest` to build a release-signed Meta Quest APK and upload it to Meta Horizon Store release channels (`alpha`, `beta`, `rc`, `store`, or subchannels) through Meta's `ovr-platform-util upload-quest-build`.

- Configures `app_id`, `channel`, `age_group` (`teens_and_adults`, `mixed_ages`, `children`), `draft`, and optional `obb`, `assets_dir`, and `debug_symbols_dir` in `[publish.quest]` with updated JSON schemas.
- Accepts `LEPTOSKIT_PUBLISH_QUEST_APP_SECRET` (preferred) or `LEPTOSKIT_PUBLISH_QUEST_TOKEN`, supports `LEPTOSKIT_OVR_PLATFORM_UTIL` overrides, redacts secrets from tool errors, and rejects x86-only ABIs before compiling.
- Defaults to `--draft` uploads until `--submit` is passed with an `age_group`, prints the remaining Meta Horizon Developer Dashboard steps (listing copy/art, Data Use Checkup, content rating, and VRC/Content review submission), and wires `quest` into the generated GitHub Actions `release.yml` workflow.

- **Multiple frontend applications in one workspace.** `leptoskit new --frontends landing,app,admin` scaffolds a `leptoskit.workspace.toml` with separate apps under `apps/` (landing and admin web-only; `app` keeps native hosts). Workspace applications may declare an optional `kind` (`landing`, `product`, `admin`, `server`) for tooling. Docs cover the multi-frontend layout; shared auth across frontends remains out of scope.
  _Owner:_ Ifiok Jr. · _Introduced in:_ [6fed659](https://github.com/leptoskit/leptoskit/commit/6fed65923cda6adbd7f8ac645ff2555ff34fb819)

#### Versioned native capability contracts

_Owner:_ Ifiok Jr. · _Introduced in:_ [442b38b](https://github.com/leptoskit/leptoskit/commit/442b38b81352231ebb9810f646247bd548ed353c)

Native builds now resolve a typed host capability descriptor from the destination flavour, the plugin registrations they actually generated, and the non-secret plugin options. `native bundle` writes `capabilities.json` beside the bundle with a stable SHA-256 digest, and the mobile host embeds the same descriptor in `codepush.json`.

`[native]` gains `required-plugins`, `optional-plugins`, `required-capabilities`, and `optional-capabilities`. A required plugin or capability the selected host cannot run fails the build before packaging, regardless of `missing-plugins`; an optional omission warns with the platform and reason. Existing `plugins` and `missing-plugins` keep their behavior when no requirement lists are set, and a capability declaration never grants access.

Signed releases carry versioned required/optional requirements in `runtime.json`. The installed host checks them against its own descriptor before staging or activating an update; unsupported, unknown, or experimental-without-opt-in requirements are refused. Releases built before this format still pass the legacy ABI, shell, and plugin checks and are reported as legacy, never as verified-compatible. Unknown contract versions and conflicting or duplicate entries are rejected.

Guest requirements bind the bridge protocol as well as the rendering ABI. Explicitly optional plugins no longer enter the legacy required-plugin list. Watch preparation checks requirements before writing its stubs and emits a descriptor; standalone bundles place host evidence beside the output directory.

Updates whose older-style plugin grants have no available implementation report `incomplete` while preserving the existing missing-plugin fallback. Explicit required entries still reject unavailable plugins; explicit optional entries may be omitted. A versioned host descriptor must agree with its own grant list before it can check a release.

Generated iOS and Android update controls show whether host requirements were checked, plugin availability remains incomplete, or only legacy checks ran. A missing report from an older runtime is shown as unreported. None of these states claims that the updated app passed device tests.

The descriptor also names `host.timer` where the generated host enables the reserved `leptoskit.timer` plugin, so `required-capabilities = ["host.timer"]` fails before packaging on hosts that run no guest and is checked by code push on older store builds.

#### An app's own fonts on every platform

_Owner:_ Ifiok Jr. · _Introduced in:_ [b4744bd](https://github.com/leptoskit/leptoskit/commit/b4744bd432011c953a8a1a932f3306b270eed0ef)

Declare the typefaces an app bundles once, in `leptoskit.toml`, and choose one with the class the web already uses:

```toml
[theme.fonts.hand]
family = "Skribble Noto Sketch"
faces = [
	{ file = "fonts/NotoSketch-Regular.ttf" },
	{ file = "fonts/NotoSketch-Bold.ttf", weight = 700 },
	{ file = "fonts/NotoSketch-Italic.ttf", style = "italic" },
]

[theme.fonts.display]
faces = [{ file = "fonts/Recursive.ttf", weight = [300, 1000] }]
```

`font-[var(--hand)]` now draws the family on the web, iOS, Android, and macOS, and every text inside the element inherits it. Faces are matched by weight and style as `@font-face` rules are, a variable face draws the weight asked for on its `wght` axis, and layout measures each label in the face that draws it.

- The build checks every declared file and stops with an error naming the `[theme.fonts]` entry and the path it looked at when a file is missing or isn't a TrueType or OpenType font.
- Native builds write `fonts.json` beside the app bundle; the generated iOS, Android, and macOS hosts register the files before their first layout. The web build writes and links `leptoskit-fonts.css`.
- `leptoskit_native::fonts` holds the manifest, the face selection, and `install` for hosts written in Rust; `NativeProps::font_family` and `TextStyle::{italic, face}` carry the choice to measurement and drawing. `font-sans`, `font-serif`, and `font-mono` now return to the system font on native platforms.
- The AppKit and UIKit backends draw and measure declared faces once installed. The host text measurer's C ABI gains the face to measure in, and `lk_fonts_install` and `lk_fonts_select` let Swift and Kotlin hosts install the manifest and choose faces exactly as layout does.
- Windows, Linux, HarmonyOS, watchOS, the terminal, and the Rust `leptoskit_android` backend still draw the system font.

#### Push-enabled hosts now work the way the notifications guide describes.

_Owner:_ Ifiok Jr. · _Introduced in:_ [7f60843](https://github.com/leptoskit/leptoskit/commit/7f60843eba43202f72117226374f71d7b4f6528d)

**Android.** The scaffold's Gradle script applies Google's services plugin by id (`apply(plugin = plugin)`); the earlier `apply(plugin)` asked Gradle for a script file of that name and failed every push-enabled build. An app scaffolded with the earlier line gets a generation error that names the one-word change. The generated messaging service is declared with the `com.google.firebase.MESSAGING_EVENT` intent filter, so Firebase delivers token refreshes to it instead of to its own default service. The manifest names a default notification channel, `leptoskit.notifications.default`, which the notifications plugin creates at startup, and the notification icon when `[app.icons] notification` generated one. Release builds get R8 keep rules for the Firebase names the plugin looks up by reflection, the plugin finds the task's listener methods on the public `Task` type, and Firebase without configuration answers `firebase-not-configured` even when its exception arrives wrapped by the reflective call.

**Android channels.** The FCM transport sends `android.channel_id` under the `leptoskit.notifications.` prefix the plugin creates channels with, so a send that names `inbox` reaches the channel the app configured as `inbox`. An id that already carries the prefix is sent unchanged.

**iOS and macOS.** The permission request asks for alerts, badges, and sounds, so a push's `aps.badge` and `aps.sound` take effect where the person allows them; it asked for alerts only.

**macOS.** A push-enabled Mac app (`[native.macos] aps-environment`) now needs `[native.macos] provisioning-profile`, a new setting naming the profile to embed: Apple's push entitlement is restricted, and macOS refuses to launch an app that claims it without a matching embedded profile. Generation stops without the profile. `leptoskit build --platform macos` embeds it at `Contents/embedded.provisionprofile` and signs with the identity in `LEPTOSKIT_MACOS_IDENTITY`, refusing to ad-hoc sign; `--release --unsigned` builds without the push entitlement. `leptoskit publish macos` embeds the profile before signing with the Developer ID identity. This follows Apple's signing rules and has not been run against a real Apple developer account. Apps without `aps-environment` generate and sign exactly as before.

**Web.** The receiver worker claims the pages already open when it activates, so a click can route the tab a person enrolled from, and a click on an action button adds the button's id to the opened address as `lka`.

The guide's samples no longer stop on iOS and macOS at `configure_channel` or enroll after a refused permission, and it now covers Web Push on iPhone and iPad needing a Home Screen install, combining the receiver with an app's own service worker, which `aps-environment` value an iOS build wants, and the entitlement a time-sensitive push needs.

- **Publish to the Solana dApp Store.** `[publish.solana]` adds Solana Mobile's store for Seeker and Saga phones to `leptoskit publish`: without `--submit` the run builds the release-signed APK with your dApp Store keystore, checks the listing text and images, the signing key (which must differ from Google Play's), the `arm64-v8a` build target, and the publishing wallet's balance (0.016 SOL minimum, through one RPC call that may only warn on an outage), and sends nothing, because Solana Mobile's official `dapp-store` tool has no draft stage; with `--submit` it runs that tool against the Publisher Portal with the APK, the wallet keypair, and "What's New" from `store/en-US/release_notes.md`, the portal API key held only in that one tool's environment. The keystore reuses the release-signing variables under `LEPTOSKIT_SOLANA_*` names, `leptoskit publish credentials` lists the six new credentials, and the generated release workflow sets up Node and decodes the keystore for it.
  _Owner:_ Ifiok Jr. · _Introduced in:_ [78d16fe](https://github.com/leptoskit/leptoskit/commit/78d16feec6021830c6a57befe95ca0eb4b06bae9)

#### `[rpc].path` and `[rpc].live_path` decide where routes serve

_Owner:_ Ifiok Jr. · _Introduced in:_ [8bd1891](https://github.com/leptoskit/leptoskit/commit/8bd1891b8d987c9abe19128343e7107d706ecd88)

`RpcConfig.path`, `live_path`, and `transports` were accepted and validated but no server read them: every app served `/rpc` and `/live` whatever the config said. Now they decide the mounts, once, at the app's entrypoint.

The generated app reads `[rpc]` from `leptoskit.toml` and applies it: operation routes serve at `path` (with the JSON routes kept on the legacy `/api` prefix while JSON is a transport), and `Server::rpc_config` carries the resolved live mount through `Server::live`. `Live` takes the same config, so a router built by hand mounts the socket at `live_path` — `/live` while the config stays at its defaults — with its server-sent events and frame posts right next to it. `path` without `live_path` moves the socket to `{path}/live`; an explicit `live_path` mounts it anywhere.

`leptoskit rpc spec` exports the configured live mount, so regenerated clients open their socket where the app serves it. Generated HTTP calls still name the compile-time `/rpc/<op>` route: keep the default `path` when generated clients call the app directly, and use a custom one behind a proxy or gateway that remounts the prefix.

#### Wearable and smartwatch support across watch OSes and BLE

_Owner:_ Ifiok Jr. · _Introduced in:_ [5b1f3ba](https://github.com/leptoskit/leptoskit/commit/5b1f3ba88e456a3bd5b427603bda36022781444d)

Adds sensor-first wearable application APIs, watch host packaging, and wearable biometric/companion/BLE plugins:

- **`leptoskit_watch`**: adds `WatchKind::HarmonyOs`, Samsung Galaxy Watch and Huawei Watch viewport presets, and the sensor-first `WearableApp` API (`WearableStream`, `SamplingPolicy`, `DeliveryMode`, `WearableStatus`, `WearableSurfaceMode::AutoStatus` / `Custom`, and per-OS `required_permissions()`).
- **`leptoskit_plugin_health`**: adds `SkinTemperature`, `ActiveCalories`, `Distance`, and `FloorsClimbed`; enables `HealthKit` on watchOS alongside iOS; adds HarmonyOS `HealthPlugin.ts` (`@kit.HealthServiceKit`).
- **`leptoskit_plugin_wearable`**: new direct on-watch live & passive biometric sensor plugin covering Wear OS Health Services (`PassiveMonitoringClient`, `MeasureClient`, `SensorManager`, plus optional Samsung Health Sensor SDK runtime hook), watchOS (`HKWorkoutSession`, `HKLiveWorkoutBuilder`, `HKObserverQuery`, `CMPedometer`), and HarmonyOS Wearable (`@kit.SensorServiceKit`).
- **`leptoskit_plugin_watch_sync`**: new bidirectional phone ↔ watch companion sync plugin over Apple `WatchConnectivity`, Android/Wear OS Wearable Data & Message Layer, and Huawei Wear Engine.
- **`leptoskit_plugin_ble`**: new BLE GATT central plugin (`CoreBluetooth`, Android/Wear OS `BluetoothGatt`, HarmonyOS `@kit.ConnectivityKit`) with pure-Rust Bluetooth SIG decoders for Heart Rate + RR-intervals/RMSSD, Pulse Oximeter (`SpO2`), Health Thermometer, Battery, Running Speed & Cadence, and Cycling Power.
- **HarmonyOS plugins**: adds ArkTS implementations for `battery`, `thermal`, and `pedometer`.
- **`leptoskit_config` & `leptoskit_cli`**: adds `[native.wearos]`, `[native.watchos]`, and `[native.harmonyos]` configuration tables; upgrades `wearos` to build Android APKs with Wear OS manifest transformation (watch feature, standalone metadata, tiles/complications); upgrades `watchos` to generate watchOS Xcode build files and invoke `xcodebuild`; updates HarmonyOS host generation to emit configured `deviceTypes` (including `"wearable"`) and `requestPermissions`.

#### Describe independently configured applications

_Owner:_ Ifiok Jr. · _Introduced in:_ [b47bc2e](https://github.com/leptoskit/leptoskit/commit/b47bc2e41920c89e7382665a7fccab1c9508de9d)

Add a separate `leptoskit.workspace.toml` manifest and `lk workspace explain` / `check`. Each application references its own configuration. Startup dependencies are validated independently of call bindings, so bidirectional calls do not become readiness cycles. Unknown references, escaping paths, repeated configurations, conflicting managed identities, and duplicate binding variables fail before a build starts.

The versioned report exposes only selected configuration and environment variable names. It explicitly marks artifacts, API compatibility, database ownership, service identity, and deployment as not checked. Workspace inspection runs no plugin programs or build tools. Image creation, binding injection, change impact, and release orchestration remain future consumers of this graph.

#### Augmented and virtual reality, and Meta Quest apps

_Owner:_ Ifiok Jr. · _Introduced in:_ [996f9b1](https://github.com/leptoskit/leptoskit/commit/996f9b1814996e5f6b3f565803d53266c3359e78)

The new `leptoskit_xr` crate and its `xr` plugin put an app in the real world. Start a session in the best mode the device has — `PhoneAr` through ARKit on iOS and ARCore on Android, `ImmersiveVr` and `ImmersiveAr` on headsets through OpenXR, WebXR in the browser, or `Orientation`, which turns the view with the phone on any device — and read a stream of frames: where the viewer is, each view's projection, the floors, tables, and walls found so far, pinned anchors, the room's light, and controllers and hands. Hit tests find where a tap or a controller's ray meets the real world, against planes and, on phones that measure it, the depth of the room. The camera and depth pictures stay in the native app for the renderer, and the frames your code receives are capped at `[native.plugin-options.xr] max-frame-rate`, always the newest. A recording replays a session exactly, for tests and simulators, with `replay = "…"`.

`leptoskit build --platform quest` builds the Android project as a Meta Quest app, with the manifest Horizon OS expects: OpenXR, head tracking, optional hand tracking and passthrough, the supported headsets, and a full-screen immersive launcher. `[native.quest]` configures it, and `leptoskit dev --platform quest` installs onto a connected headset.

With the `3d` feature, `host::scene3d::draw` draws a `leptoskit_3d` scene into a session: the camera picture behind it, real-world depth hiding what is behind real things, and one view per eye on a headset.

The backends build for their platforms but have not yet run on a device, so treat them as experimental.

sections.title: Fixes
entries:
- **Keep graph placement separate from application frontends.** Graph artifact placement uses `[infra.frontends.<name>]`. Application build frontends keep their existing top-level `[frontends.<name>]` contract. This avoids colliding configuration types when named application targets and deployment graphs are used in the same toolkit. Graph unit identifiers such as `frontends.docs` and all ownership, route and recovery checks are unchanged.
  _Owner:_ Ifiok Jr. · _Introduced in:_ [7c788ae](https://github.com/leptoskit/leptoskit/commit/7c788ae0d8522dc8f0576961ef4bcb9121603f70)

- **More ergonomic multi-frontend scaffold.** `--frontends` alone scaffolds landing, app, and admin. Ports are stable per kind. The product app under `apps/app` uses the workspace name as its Cargo package. Frontend names trim whitespace and accept ASCII case; `ApplicationKind` gains `FromStr`, `Display`, and helpers used by the scaffold. Each frontend app uses the same file-router defaults as a normal `leptoskit new`.
  _Owner:_ Ifiok Jr. · _Introduced in:_ [fa8c81a](https://github.com/leptoskit/leptoskit/commit/fa8c81afb142de65ec3b1f0908c787ac164cb306)

#### Accept managed registries with explicit ports

_Owner:_ Ifiok Jr. · _Introduced in:_ [b47bc2e](https://github.com/leptoskit/leptoskit/commit/b47bc2e41920c89e7382665a7fccab1c9508de9d)

Managed image configuration accepts a registry hostname with a numeric port and an image repository under that registry. Invalid ports, embedded credentials, paths in registry authorities, and tagged image repositories remain rejected.

Verified image packaging accepts `--service <infra.name>` to include Kamal’s required service label in the independently pinned image configuration. Reusing an image checks the label along with the rest of that configuration.

Deployment accepts Docker’s null defaults for absent Podman `Cmd`, `OnBuild`, and `Volumes` inspection fields while still requiring the exact content-addressed image ID. Non-null changes remain rejected.

#### Immersive sessions from Meta Quest panel apps

_Owner:_ Ifiok Jr. · _Introduced in:_ [e897f31](https://github.com/leptoskit/leptoskit/commit/e897f31c27dbc9cb0c39378f56f705e9ef8e83f8)

A Quest app now draws its 3D scene into the headset. Start an `ImmersiveVr` or `ImmersiveAr` session and choose the scene with the new `Session::present(Some(scene_id))`: each eye sees the scene from the player's eye, over passthrough in `ImmersiveAr`. An app built with `[native.quest] immersive = false`, a 2D panel, opens an immersive activity over the panel for the session and comes back to the panel in Horizon Home when the session ends, while its code keeps running and receiving frames.

`leptoskit build --platform quest` declares that activity in every Quest app, marks a panel app's launcher with Horizon OS's 2D category and targets Horizon OS v69, and turns on `leptoskit_xr`'s new `quest` feature (or any async plugin's `quest` feature). For hosts that draw scenes themselves, `leptoskit_3d::host::Hub::draw_scene` draws a scene on another device, such as a headset's, and `Hub::forget_device` moves scenes off it again.

None of this has run on a headset yet.

## [0.3.1](https://github.com/leptoskit/leptoskit/releases/tag/v0.3.1) (2026-11-28)

### Features

- **`[native.android] push` opts the Android app into FCM push enrollment.** It is a boolean, off by default: an app without it generates byte-for-byte as before. With it, Android generation adds the pinned `com.google.firebase:firebase-messaging` dependency, writes `.leptoskit/android/gradle-plugins.txt` with Google's services plugin, generates the messaging service that forwards FCM token refreshes to the notifications plugin, and declares that service in the manifest. Push on also requires the `notifications` plugin in `[native] plugins`, the app author's `google-services.json` at `hosts/android/app/google-services.json` — never generated or committed by leptoskit — and an app Gradle script that reads the generated plugins file (the current `leptoskit new` scaffold does; older apps get the exact lines from the generation error). The configuration schema carries the new key.
  _Owner:_ Ifiok Jr. · _Introduced in:_ [b782f13](https://github.com/leptoskit/leptoskit/commit/b782f1372a8b11ae1338a003c937282609188021)

- Adds `--web-only` and `--cloud` flags to `lk new` and `lk generate app`, allows `--frontends` to combine with `--db`, `--auth`, `--web-only`, and `--cloud`, and falls back with a clear warning instead of hard-failing `lk dev` when `monosecret` is not installed.
- Exposes six cloud and database tools on `lk mcp` (`cloud_estimate`, `cloud_deploy`, `cloud_status`, `cloud_logs`, `cloud_secrets_list`, `db_check`) without ever returning secret values.

- **The groundwork for LeptosKit Cloud.** `leptoskit.toml` accepts a `[cloud]` table that says where LeptosKit Cloud should run your app and how big: a project, an optional region, and per-environment size, replicas, sleeping when idle and custom domains, plus the database's size and backups. Config checks it as it loads, with errors that name the table and key, such as a SQLite app asking for more than one replica, or sleeping while it serves live queries. The new `leptoskit_cloud` crate holds the shared types behind it: slugs, sizes, deployment states, the source archive a deploy will upload (deterministic, with secret files refused), and a monthly cost estimate for a `[cloud]` table. The cloud itself doesn't run yet, so nothing deploys there today.
